docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
The backend is a FastAPI app (backend/app/main.py). Every endpoint is under /api except /health and /health/agents. A running instance serves Swagger UI at /docs, ReDoc at /redoc and the schema at /openapi.json; locally that is http://localhost:8001/docs.

Authentication. Send the token from POST /api/auth/login as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Tokens are HS256 JWTs valid for 24 hours. In the tables below:

  • user: a valid token for an active user is required (401 otherwise).
  • admin: the user must also be an admin (403 otherwise).
  • optional: anonymous calls are allowed. With a valid token for an active user, the Taste Graph is applied and rate limits count per user; otherwise (including a deactivated user's token) the caller is anonymous and counted per IP.
  • none: no token needed.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
Endpoints that call the AI agents are rate-limited per caller (the signed-in user, or the client IP for anonymous requests) over a sliding 10-minute window (backend/app/core/rate_limit.py). Every accepted request counts, including cached responses and requests later rejected as invalid (422) or unauthenticated (401); only requests answered with 429 do not.

Bucket Endpoints Default limit search POST /api/search, POST /api/search/sync 10 chat POST /api/chat 30 compare POST /api/compare/destination 30 discover POST /api/discover 10 light_ai POST /api/flights, /hotels, /activities and their /filtered variants, /flights/fare-calendar, /visa, /sim, /tips, /getting-around, /forex, /itinerary, /events, /walking-tours, /layover, /stress-test 60

Each bucket is counted separately. Over the limit the API answers 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds) and:

{"detail": "Too many requests — please wait 42 seconds and try again."}

Limits are configurable (see Configuration). The counter is in-process, so each backend process counts on its own.

docs.title: POST /api/auth/login
docs.text:
{ "username": "admin", "password": "your-password" }

Response (401 for wrong credentials or an inactive account):

{
  "access_token": "eyJ...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "user": { "username": "admin", "is_admin": true, "requires_password_change": false }
}

If requires_password_change is true, the frontend sends the user to /change-password first.

docs.title: POST /api/auth/change-password
docs.text:
{ "current_password": "old", "new_password": "at-least-8-chars" }

Returns {"access_token": "...", "token_type": "bearer"} with a fresh token. 400 if the current password is wrong or the new one is shorter than 8 characters.

docs.title: GET /api/auth/me
docs.text:
Returns { "username", "is_admin", "requires_password_change" }.

There is no registration endpoint. Admins create users:

docs.title: POST /api/admin/users
docs.text:
{ "username": "newuser", "password": "TemporaryPassword123", "email": null, "is_admin": false }

201 with the user (no password hash). The new user must change the password on first login. 409 for a duplicate username or email, 400 for a password under 8 characters. POST /api/admin/users/{username}/reset-password takes {"new_password": "..."}.

docs.title: POST /api/search
docs.text:
The main endpoint. It streams results as Server-Sent Events. Auth: optional. Responses for a complete, error-free run are cached for 30 minutes and replayed instantly.

Request body (TravelSearchRequest, backend/app/schemas/request.py):

{
  "origin": "London",
  "destination": "Tokyo",
  "departure_date": "2026-06-01",
  "return_date": "2026-06-14",
  "nationality": "British",
  "interests": ["food", "history", "nature"],
  "budget_usd": 4000,
  "num_travelers": 2,
  "adults": 2, "children": 0, "seniors": 0, "infants": 0,
  "accessibility_needs": [],
  "residence_permits": [],
  "existing_visas": [],
  "destinations": null,
  "destination_nights": null,
  "pace": "balanced",
  "serendipity": 0.5
}

destinations and destination_nights describe a multi-city trip (see Multi-City Trips). taste_context is set by the server from the user's Taste Graph; a client value is ignored. origin and destination may be city names, typeahead labels or airport codes; the validator resolves them to airport codes for live flight search (see Place and Airport Data).

Response: Content-Type: text/event-stream. Each event is data: {JSON}\n\n, and : keepalive comments are sent while agents run.

Event Phase source Notes visa, sim, tips, getting_around, forex 0, then 1 static, then ai Static-backed; an AI error is not sent, so the static data stays confidence 0 static Travel Ease grade: total out of 100 and green/amber/red, from visa ease, safety, English friendliness, cost vs budget and tourist infrastructure emergency_card 0, then 1 static, then ai Static-backed agent_status — — {agent, status: "searching" \| "done"} for the 15 agents at start, and for stress_test flights, weather, hotels, activities, places_to_see, walking_tours, events 1 ai hotels, activities and places_to_see are sent twice: before and after link enrichment packing_list deferred ai (static for the template fallback) Starts when activities and weather are in pricing_advisor deferred ai Starts when flights have at least 3 results; skipped on error or after 120 s itinerary 2 none Starts when activities and hotels are in; template fallback after 60 s stress_test after the itinerary ai 90 s timeout; on error an error section is sent done — — Always last

Every non-error section carries data.verification (see Agent System). An agent that fails sends {"error": "..."} as its data (except the static-backed ones), so the UI can show "not available" instead of waiting.

docs.title: POST /api/search/sync
docs.text: Same request and agents, run sequentially; returns a single JSON object. For testing only.

docs.title: POST /api/discover
docs.text:
Surprise me. Auth: optional. Returns 5 destination suggestions.

{
  "origin": "JFK",
  "nationality": "American",
  "departure_date": "2026-08-01",
  "return_date": "2026-08-08",
  "budget_usd": 3000,
  "interests": ["food", "history"],
  "adults": 1, "children": 0, "seniors": 0, "infants": 0
}

return_date and budget_usd are optional. Response:

{
  "destinations": [
    {
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "country": "Portugal",
      "estimated_cost_usd_low": 1400,
      "estimated_cost_usd_high": 2200,
      "visa_type": "visa-free",
      "visa_verified": true,
      "weather_emoji": "☀️",
      "weather_description": "Warm and sunny, 22–26°C in August",
      "flight_duration_hours": 7.5,
      "flight_duration_label": "~7h 30m from New York",
      "match_reasons": ["Exceptional food scene", "Rich Age of Discovery history"],
      "highlights": ["Alfama district", "Sintra", "Belém Tower"]
    }
  ]
}

visa_verified: true means the visa type came from the static visa table; otherwise it is the model's guess and the UI shows a warning badge. Errors: 422 invalid request, 504 after 30 s, 500 agent failure. Results are cached for 30 minutes.

docs.title: POST /api/compare/destination
docs.text:
Lightweight summary of one destination, used by the Search page's Compare mode (one call per destination, in parallel). Runs flights, hotels (no URL enrichment), weather and visa concurrently with per-piece timeouts (flights and hotels 45 s, weather and visa 30 s). The visa piece uses the static visa table when it has an entry.

Auth: user. Bucket: compare.

Request body: a TravelSearchRequest for a single destination. destinations must be null or have at most one entry; multi-city requests return 422 ("Compare works with single destinations").

Response (200) — example for 2 adults, 7 nights, budget_usd: 3000:

{
  "destination": "Lisbon, Portugal",
  "label": "Lisbon",
  "flight": {"price_usd": 620, "stops": 0, "duration_minutes": 895, "airline": "TAP Air Portugal", "source": "google_flights"},
  "hotel": {"typical_nightly_usd": 110, "cheapest_good_nightly_usd": 70, "count": 5},
  "weather": {"avg_high_c": 24.4, "avg_low_c": 15.7, "poor_days": 1, "total_days": 7, "source": "open-meteo"},
  "visa": {"visa_type": "visa-free", "max_stay_days": 90, "fee_usd": 0, "processing_time": "Not required", "verified": true},
  "ease": {"total": 80, "grade": "green", "safety": 18, "english": 15, "infrastructure": 17, "visa_ease": 10},
  "daily_cost_usd": 100,
  "estimate": {
    "total_usd": 1320,
    "flight_usd": 620,
    "stay_usd": 385,
    "daily_usd": 700,
    "included_in_daily": true,
    "nights": 7,
    "partial": false,
    "budget_status": "under"
  },
  "missing": []
}

Any piece that failed or timed out is null and its name is listed in missing; ease/daily_cost_usd are null for destinations outside the static tables. flight.source of estimate marks a non-live fare; visa.verified is true only for static-table data. ease.grade is green (≥ 71), amber (41–70) or red (≤ 40).

Estimate (per traveller): flight_usd is the cheapest fare (flight.price_usd, round trip, per person). daily_usd = daily_cost_usd × days (days = nights, min 1; nights default to 7 without a return_date). daily_cost_usd is an all-in daily budget that already includes lodging, so when it is known total_usd = flight_usd + daily_usd and stay_usd is shown for reference only (included_in_daily: true) — above, 620 + 700 = 1320. When the daily figure is unknown, total_usd = flight_usd + stay_usd and included_in_daily is false. stay_usd = typical nightly × nights × rooms ÷ travellers, with rooms = ⌈(adults + seniors) ÷ 2⌉ (falling back to ⌈num_travelers ÷ 2⌉) — above, 110 × 7 × 1 ÷ 2 = 385. partial is true when the flight or the daily figure is unknown; the total then sums only the known parts. budget_status compares total_usd × num_travelers with budget_usd (the party's budget): over, under (only for a complete estimate), or null with no budget or when a partial total is still within it.

Errors: 422 for multi-city or invalid requests; 502 when every piece failed.

Caching: only complete results (empty missing) are cached in the shared TTL cache, keyed on the full request; partial results and 502s are never cached.

docs.title: POST /api/chat
docs.text:
Auth: user. Streams SSE.

{
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Plan a 5-day trip to Bangkok for two people" }],
  "selections": {},
  "search_results": {},
  "session_context": {}
}

Event types: delta (text), done, error, suggestions, session_context_update, plan_action, planning_start, trip_map, itinerary_generating, comprehensive_itinerary, planning_done, agent_status and section_result. A planning request streams planning_start → trip_map → itinerary_generating → comprehensive_itinerary → planning_done; section_result appears only in the specialist fallback and refinement paths. An exception still ends the stream with a fallback delta, error and done. See Chat Assistant.

docs.text: Get, update (name and/or selections) or delete one of the caller's plans; 404 for another user's plan.

docs.title: POST /api/plans/{id}/share and GET /api/share/{token}
docs.text: POST returns {"share_token": "..."} (the existing token if there is one). GET /api/share/{token} needs no auth and returns the plan's name, timestamps, selections and only these search fields: origin, destination, destinations, dates, interests, traveller counts and pace. DELETE /api/plans/{id}/share revokes the token. See Sharing and Plans.

docs.title: GET, PUT /api/preferences
docs.text: The caller's preferences: budget_category, nationality, current_residence, residence_permits, existing_visas, interests, num_travelers, adults, children, seniors, infants, accessibility_needs. They pre-fill the Search form, and the Search form writes back to them.

docs.title: GET, POST /api/recent-searches; DELETE /api/recent-searches/{id}
docs.text: GET returns the caller's last 8 searches, newest first, each { "id", "search", "last_used_at" }, where search is the Search form as submitted (route with multi-city stops and optional nights, dates, nationality, permits, visas, interests, budget, traveller mix, accessibility needs, serendipity). POST records one: an identical search (interests in any order) is moved back to the top instead of duplicated, and only the newest 8 are kept. DELETE returns 204, or 404 if the entry does not exist or belongs to someone else.

docs.title: GET, DELETE /api/taste-profile
docs.text: GET returns the learned signals (flight style, hotel tier, activity categories, budget band) and the summary injected into agent prompts. DELETE resets them.

docs.title: POST /api/feedback
docs.text:
{ "page": "results", "rating": 4, "category": "praise", "message": "Great activity suggestions!" }

rating is 1–5; category is bug, feature_request, general or praise; message (optional) is at most 500 characters; metadata is an optional object. Returns 201. Admins read feedback with GET /api/admin/feedback?page=&category=&min_rating=.

docs.title: POST /api/analytics/events
docs.text: Up to 50 batched UI events per call, written to the log as JSON. Returns 204.

docs.title: Single-agent and helper endpoints
docs.text:
Each takes the TravelSearchRequest body of /api/search unless noted. Auth: optional (except the fare calendar). Bucket: light_ai.

Endpoint Returns POST /api/flights Flight options; multi-city returns ordered legs. Live single-city results may carry price_insights POST /api/flights/filtered Flights with max_stops, max_price_usd, departure_time_earliest/latest, arrival_time_earliest/latest; enriched and verification-labelled POST /api/hotels Hotels across budget tiers POST /api/hotels/filtered Hotels with num_beds, max_price_per_night_usd, wifi_quality, max_distance_from_center_km, private_washroom POST /api/activities Interest-ranked activities POST /api/activities/filtered Activities with filter_interests, max_price_usd, available_from/to, min_rating POST /api/visa, /api/sim, /api/tips, /api/getting-around, /api/forex The corresponding specialist result POST /api/itinerary Day-by-day itinerary POST /api/events What's On during the trip POST /api/walking-tours Crawled free walking tours (see below) POST /api/layover Layover plan. Own body: city, duration_hours (> 0, ≤ 48), nationality, optional airport, arrival_time (HH:MM) and interests POST /api/stress-test Audit of an itinerary. Body: the search request plus itinerary (required) and optional flights, visa and weather

docs.title: Flight price_insights
docs.text:
When flights come from Google Flights (SerpAPI) on a single-city trip, the result may include Google's own price verdict, taken from the outbound search response (no extra calls). Fields are kept only when well-formed; the object is omitted when there is no usable price_level or lowest_price. Model-generated flight results never carry it (stripped like live_fare), and it does not change the section's verification label.

"price_insights": {
  "lowest_price": 512,
  "price_level": "low",
  "typical_price_range": [600, 820],
  "price_history": [[1727740800, 650], [1727827200, 512]]
}

price_level is low, typical or high.

docs.title: POST /api/flights/fare-calendar
docs.text:
Auth required (401 without a valid token); light_ai rate-limit bucket. Body: the same TravelSearchRequest as /api/search.

For each departure date from 3 days before to 3 days after the requested one, it makes one Google Flights outbound search (SerpAPI) with the return date shifted by the same amount, so the trip length stays the same, and takes the cheapest price (for a round trip that is already the round-trip total). There are no return-leg calls, so this is at most 7 calls, run 4 at a time. Overlapping requests for the same dates (a second tab, a double-mounted component) share the lookups already in flight, so each date costs one call. Dates before tomorrow are skipped. An unfiltered main flight search stores its own cheapest outbound-stage price as the calendar entry for its dates. The requested date shows the lower of that price and the cheapest flight card of the cached main search, so it matches the cards (the main round-trip search always return-prices the lowest-priced outbound, wherever Google lists it, plus the earliest and latest departures); Google's price_insights.lowest_price is used only when neither is available. Each date's price is cached for 30 minutes (serp-cal:{origin}:{dest}:{dep}:{ret}:{travelers}). A date that fails for any reason (HTTP error, timeout, unreadable response) or has no flights comes back as null; the calendar as a whole never fails, and failures are not cached.

{
  "dates": [
    {"departure_date": "2026-10-31", "return_date": "2026-11-07", "cheapest_usd": 610.0, "is_selected": false},
    {"departure_date": "2026-11-03", "return_date": "2026-11-10", "cheapest_usd": 565.0, "is_selected": true},
    {"departure_date": "2026-11-04", "return_date": "2026-11-11", "cheapest_usd": null, "is_selected": false}
  ],
  "currency": "USD",
  "source": "google_flights"
}

Errors (string detail):

Status When 401 Not signed in 422 Multi-city request ("Fare calendar is only available for single-destination trips.") or invalid body 429 Rate limit (see above) 503 {"detail": "Fare calendar needs live flight data, which isn't configured."} — SERPAPI_KEY is not set

docs.title: POST /api/walking-tours
docs.text:
Free and pay-what-you-wish walking tours at the destination (every stop on multi-city trips). Tours are crawled from the providers' public city pages; the LLM only chooses and explains them by id, so every url is a real provider tour page. Same request body as /api/search.

{
  "origin": "NYC",
  "destination": "Lisbon, Portugal",
  "departure_date": "2026-04-01",
  "return_date": "2026-04-08",
  "interests": ["history", "food"],
  "num_travelers": 2
}

Response:

{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "t3",
      "name": "Lisbon Old Town Free Walking Tour",
      "provider": "GuruWalk",
      "provider_key": "guruwalk",
      "url": "https://www.guruwalk.com/walks/...",
      "image_url": "https://...",
      "description": "Alfama, the cathedral and the viewpoints, with a local guide.",
      "rating": 4.9,
      "review_count": 1280,
      "duration": "2h 30m",
      "price_note": "Free (tip your guide)",
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "reason": "Covers the old-town history you asked for.",
      "top_pick": true
    }
  ],
  "sources": [
    {
      "provider": "GuruWalk",
      "provider_key": "guruwalk",
      "city": "Lisbon",
      "url": "https://www.guruwalk.com/lisbon",
      "count": 6,
      "status": "ok"
    }

}

sources has one entry per provider and city; status is ok, none (page found, no free tours) or error. Each city is topped up to at least min(4, available) tours. The endpoint returns {"error": ...} only when every provider fails.

docs.text: Airport and place typeahead (limit 1–50, default 10). Matches airport codes, cities, names and countries, plus GeoNames places and curated hints by folded name prefix ("kyoto" → ITM, KIX; "milan" → MXP, LIN, BGY). Rows: iata_code, name, city, country, country_code. Ordering and rules: Place and Airport Data.

docs.title: GET /api/nationalities/search?q=&limit=
docs.text: Nationality typeahead over 202 seeded rows.

docs.text: {"status": "ok", "service": "travel-planner-backend", "serpapi_configured": true|false}. No auth. The Results page reads serpapi_configured once per page load to decide whether to offer the fare calendar; Docker Compose uses this endpoint as the backend healthcheck.

docs.title: Agent System
docs.text: How agents are defined and executed, what each one does, and how static data and verification wrap around them.

docs.title: Agent definitions
docs.text:
Each agent's system prompt lives in .agents/<name>.md at the repo root: YAML frontmatter with name and description, followed by the prompt body.

---
name: flights
description: Expert flight search specialist — finds available round-trip flights ...
---

You are a flight search specialist...

backend/app/agents/loader.py reads the file into an AgentDefinition(name, description, system_prompt). The directory comes from AGENTS_DIR (default <repo>/.agents). Changing an agent's behaviour usually means editing its prompt; the Python class builds the user prompt and post-processes the JSON.

There are 22 definition files:

.agents file Python class (backend/app/agents/) Used by flights.md flights_agent.py search, /flights, compare, chat fallback weather.md weather_agent.py search, compare hotels.md hotels_agent.py search, /hotels, compare, chat activities.md activities_agent.py search, /activities, chat places.md places_agent.py search (places_to_see) walking_tours.md walking_tours_agent.py search, /walking-tours events.md events_agent.py search, /events, chat warnings visa.md visa_agent.py search, /visa, compare, chat sim.md sim_agent.py search, /sim, chat tips.md tips_agent.py search, /tips, chat emergency_card.md emergency_card_agent.py search getting-around.md getting_around_agent.py search, /getting-around, chat forex.md forex_agent.py search, /forex packing_list.md packing_list_agent.py search (deferred) pricing_advisor.md pricing_advisor_agent.py search (deferred) itinerary.md itinerary_agent.py search Phase 2, /itinerary stress_test.md stress_test_agent.py search (after the itinerary), /stress-test discovery.md discovery_agent.py /discover layover.md layover_agent.py /layover chat.md chat_agent.py /chat chat-itinerary.md chat_itinerary_agent.py chat comprehensive planning orchestrator.md none Descriptive only; the orchestrator is the Python TravelOrchestrator

docs.title: Execution: BaseAgent
docs.text:
backend/app/agents/base_agent.py:

  • One API call per attempt. execute(prompt) calls AsyncAnthropic.messages.create with model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, max_tokens 16384, the definition's prompt as the system prompt (plus "Return ONLY valid JSON") and the agent's prompt as the single user message. No tools are passed to the model.
  • Concurrency. A global semaphore limits concurrent calls to AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 6), so a burst of agents does not trip the organisation's rate limits. The SDK client also retries 3 times on its own.
  • Retries. Up to 4 attempts. Rate-limit, overload and connection errors back off min(2^n, 10) seconds; other errors back off 2n seconds.
  • Token cap. If a response stops at max_tokens, the next attempt adds a "be compact" instruction instead of repeating the same request.
  • JSON parsing (_parse_json), three strategies: parse the whole text, extract a fenced code block, then take the outermost {...}.
  • Failure. After the last attempt the agent returns {"error": "..."} rather than raising.

ToolAgent (a BaseAgent subclass) adds enrich(data), which the orchestrator runs in the background after the first result has streamed; a changed result is streamed again. Flights (LLM results only), hotels, activities, places, visa, sim, tips, getting around and forex override it to look up real links (DuckDuckGo through web_tools.py, at most 4 concurrent searches; Serper as a second tier for activities and places when SERPER_KEY is set). Only hotels, activities and places_to_see mark their first yield as verification-pending.

Every specialist subclass overrides run(request) to build its user prompt and post-process the result. No agent has its own API plumbing.

docs.title: The specialists
docs.text:
Flights. With SERPAPI_KEY, live Google Flights results via SerpAPI (services/serp_flights.py), marked live_fare; single-city results may carry Google's price_insights. Multi-city trips search one leg at a time (see Multi-City Trips). Without a key, or for legs SerpAPI cannot serve, the LLM produces estimates.

Weather. Open-Meteo forecast when the trip starts within 16 days and the city has coordinates (utils/geo.py), otherwise an LLM seasonal estimate. Multi-city trips get a forecast per stay.

Hotels. Options across budget tiers (luxury, premium, mid-range, budget); links are searched and checked during enrichment.

Activities. Activities matched to the traveller's interests. The model itself assigns each activity a relevance similarity_score; there is no embedding model in the code base.

Places to See. Landmarks and sights. With SERPER_KEY, Google Places data from Serper is passed to the model; otherwise the model works alone.

Free Walking Tours. services/walking_tours.py crawls the public city pages of GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, FreeWalkingTour.com and SANDEMANs NewEurope (free and pay-what-you-wish tours only; cached per provider and city). The LLM only picks and explains tours by candidate id, so every URL comes from the crawl. Each city is topped up to at least min(4, available) tours; if the LLM fails, a rating-and-reviews ranking is used.

Events (What's On). Festivals, concerts and markets during the dates. A ~ on a date marks a typical-season estimate.

Visa, SIM, Tips, Getting Around, Forex. Static-backed (see below). Forex runs several DuckDuckGo searches for current rates in parallel and has the model extract them.

Emergency Card. Per-city police, ambulance and fire numbers, the traveller's embassy (skipped for home-country cities), hospitals, survival phrases and local laws. The frontend can print it.

Packing List (deferred). Starts when activities and weather are both in; a template list is used after 120 s or on error.

Pricing Advisor (deferred). Starts once flights have at least 3 results; gives booking-timing advice and the data for the sparkline in the Flights section. Skipped after 120 s or on error.

Itinerary. Day-by-day plan with morning, afternoon and evening slots, each with duration_hours and lat/lng, which the frontend uses to derive estimated times. Template fallback after 60 s.

Stress Test. Audits the final itinerary against flights, visa and weather: pacing, timings, visa deadlines, weather clashes. Also callable with an edited itinerary through POST /api/stress-test (the "Re-check" button).

Discovery. Powers Surprise me (POST /api/discover): five destinations with cost range, weather, visa type, flight time and match reasons. The visa type is replaced by the static visa table when it has an entry; otherwise it is shown as unverified. 30 s timeout (504), cached.

Layover. A mini-plan for a long connection (POST /api/layover, up to 48 h).

Chat and Chat-Itinerary. See Chat Assistant.

docs.title: Static data and fallbacks
docs.text:
backend/app/agents/static_results.py holds curated tables:

Table Entries Feeds _VISA_TABLE 34 (nationality, destination) pairs Phase 0 visa, visa verification, discovery and compare visa _DESTINATION_SCORES 49 Travel Ease grade (get_confidence_score), daily cost _EMERGENCY_NUMBERS 40 Phase 0 emergency card, emergency verification _CITY_TO_COUNTRY 204 Matching a destination to a table country _GLOBAL_ESIMS / _LOCAL_SIMS 4 / 10 countries Phase 0 SIM _UNIVERSAL_TIPS / _DESTINATION_TIPS universal + 6 countries Phase 0 tips _GETTING_AROUND_TABLE 13 Phase 0 getting around _FOREX_TABLE, _DEST_CURRENCY, _NATIONALITY_TO_CURRENCY 6, 52, 37 Phase 0 forex

Six agents are static-backed: visa, sim, tips, getting_around, forex and emergency_card. Phase 0 sends their static result; Phase 1 replaces it with the AI result; if the AI fails, the error is suppressed and the static data stays. Phase 0 also sends a confidence event with the Travel Ease grade.

Matching a destination to a table country (_place_country) uses whole names only, never substrings. A stated country wins. Otherwise the city map is used, including St/Saint variants and city aliases, and checked against a stated region or ISO code ("Miami, FL", "Perth, WA", "Berlin, DE", "Cartagena, ES" → Spain). A city not in the map falls back to the GeoNames place resolver ("Zermatt" → Switzerland), then to unique region names or codes, then to "City Country" written without a comma.

docs.title: Source verification
docs.text:
The orchestrator attaches data.verification to every non-error section just before yielding it (attach_verification in backend/app/services/verification.py); the filtered endpoints attach the same final label. The function is pure: it uses only evidence already in the data and never calls the network or an LLM. The object never contains an error key, so it cannot trip the cache's error guard.

Section Evidence Rule flights live_fare on options mapped from SerpAPI (never trusted from LLM output) all live → verified; some → partial; none → unverified hotels link_verified from enrichment: a search result whose title or path contains the hotel's distinctive name words counted over the hotels actually searched activities, places_to_see link_checked on every item the resolvers searched; link_verified when a trusted result's title contains the item's distinctive name words "1 of the 5 checked were found online by name" walking_tours crawl provenance verified weather source: "open-meteo" verified; LLM estimates unverified visa compared with the static visa table match → verified; different visa type → conflict; no entry → unverified emergency_card compared with the static emergency numbers verified only when at least 2 of police/ambulance/fire were compared and all matched; any mismatch → conflict sim, tips, getting_around, forex (Phase 0 yields) curated reference data verified everything else (AI yields of the above, itinerary, stress test, packing list, pricing advisor) none unverified

Name matching (services/name_match.py) drops destination words and generic words ("hotel", "tour", "museum", …) first, so "Berlin City Tour" is not evidence for a "Top Berlin Tours" page. The first, pre-enrichment yield of hotels, activities and places is pending: true; the frontend clears a still-pending label when the stream ends. Model-supplied link_verified and link_checked flags are stripped, and saved plans drop them.

docs.title: Adding an agent
docs.text:
1. Create .agents/<name>.md with name and description frontmatter and the system prompt.
  2. Create backend/app/agents/<name>_agent.py: subclass BaseAgent (or ToolAgent if it needs link enrichment), load the definition, and implement run(request).
  3. Wire it into TravelOrchestrator (backend/app/agents/orchestrator.py) in the right phase, and add a route under backend/app/api/routes/ if it should be callable alone (add the light_ai rate-limit dependency in main.py).
  4. If the section should be labelled, add a rule to verify_section in services/verification.py; otherwise it is "AI-generated".
  5. Frontend: add the event type to AGENT_ORDER / the agent config in frontend/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx and write the section component.
  6. Add tests under backend/tests/ (the agent classes are excluded from coverage, so test the parsing and orchestration paths directly).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: How Travel Planner fits together, from a submitted search to the last section on screen.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Browser (React 18 SPA, Vite)
  ├── sseWorker.js  ── POST /api/search  (SSE)
  ├── chatWorker.js ── POST /api/chat    (SSE)
  └── axios         ── everything else  (JSON)
            │
            ▼
FastAPI backend (uvicorn, one process)
  ├── middleware: CORS, request logging, X-Request-ID
  ├── routers: one per domain, rate-limit dependency on AI routes
  ├── TravelOrchestrator ── Phase 0 static tables
  │                       ├── Phase 1: 13 specialist agents in parallel (+2 deferred)
  │                       └── Phase 2: itinerary → stress test
  ├── ChatAgent ── routing, knowledge answers, comprehensive planning
  ├── services: SerpAPI flights, Serper places, link resolvers,
  │             walking-tour crawler, verification, compare
  ├── TTLCache (in memory, 30 min)
  └── SQLite: $DATA_DIR/airports.db (12 tables) ── optional GCS backup every 60 s
            │
            ▼
External: Anthropic API (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6), SerpAPI, Serper, DuckDuckGo,
          Open-Meteo, walking-tour provider sites

In the container setup, nginx serves the built frontend and proxies /api/ and /health to the backend.

docs.title: The search pipeline
docs.text: POST /api/search (backend/app/api/routes/search.py) checks the cache, then streams TravelOrchestrator.stream_run() (backend/app/agents/orchestrator.py).

docs.title: Phase 0: static data (instant)
docs.text: Lookup tables in backend/app/agents/static_results.py produce, in this order: visa, sim, tips, getting_around and forex; then a confidence event (the Travel Ease grade); then emergency_card. All carry source: "static", and the UI marks those sections "Enhancing…" until the AI version arrives.

docs.title: Phase 1: thirteen agents in parallel
docs.text:
flights, weather, hotels, activities, places_to_see, walking_tours, events, visa, sim, tips, emergency_card, getting_around and forex start together. Each has a 240 s ceiling. A section is yielded as soon as its agent finishes, with source: "ai".

  • Static-backed agents (visa, sim, tips, getting_around, forex, emergency_card): if the AI result is an error, it is not yielded, so the Phase 0 data stays. The frontend also refuses to replace valid data with an error.
  • URL enrichment: hotels, activities and places_to_see are yielded first with verification.pending = true, then again after their links have been searched and checked.
  • Deferred agents: packing_list starts once activities and weather are both in (template fallback after 120 s or on error). pricing_advisor starts once flights have at least 3 results (skipped after 120 s or on error).

docs.title: Phase 2: itinerary and stress test
docs.text:
The itinerary agent starts as soon as activities and hotels are both in, not after all of Phase 1. After 60 s, or on an empty or malformed result, a template itinerary built from the available activities is used instead. Once the itinerary is final, the stress-test agent audits it (pacing, timings, visa deadlines, weather clashes) with a 90 s timeout.

The stream always ends with {"type": "done"}. While agents run, the server sends : keepalive comments.

POST /api/search/sync runs the same agents sequentially and returns one JSON object; it is meant for testing.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: A complete, error-free run is stored as its list of SSE events in the TTL cache for 30 minutes, keyed by the md5 of the request JSON (which includes the user's Taste Graph context), and replayed instantly on a repeat. Runs with any error are never cached.

docs.title: SSE envelope
docs.text:
data: {"type": "visa", "data": {...}, "source": "static"}

data: {"type": "agent_status", "agent": "flights", "status": "searching"}

data: {"type": "flights", "data": {..., "verification": {...}}, "source": "ai"}

data: {"type": "itinerary", "data": {...}}

data: {"type": "done"}

The full list of event types is in API Reference. The frontend parses the stream in a Web Worker (frontend/src/workers/sseWorker.js) so that large JSON payloads do not block rendering. If the stream ends without done, the worker reports an interruption and the page says so.

docs.title: Source verification
docs.text: Every non-error section streamed by /api/search, and the responses of /api/{flights,hotels,activities}/filtered, carry data.verification: {level, label, summary, checks[], items_verified, items_total, pending}. backend/app/services/verification.py computes it from evidence the pipeline already holds: live SerpAPI fares, link checks from enrichment, crawl provenance, Open-Meteo provenance, and comparisons with the static visa and emergency tables. It makes no network or LLM calls. The levels are verified ("Verified"), partial ("Partly verified"), unverified ("AI-generated") and conflict ("Check details"). See Agent System for the per-section rules. Chat does not use verification.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Use Model Every specialist agent (BaseAgent), the chat-itinerary agent, chat routing, parameter extraction and plan actions, /health/agents claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 Chat conversational answers and planning narrative claude-sonnet-4-6

BaseAgent.execute() makes one AsyncAnthropic.messages.create call per attempt with max_tokens 16384, behind a global semaphore (AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENCY, default 6). See Agent System.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
There is one SQLite file, $DATA_DIR/airports.db (backend/app/db/database.py), opened in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL and a 5 s busy timeout. Despite its name it holds every table:

Table Holds airports Airports from OurAirports plus the curated list (IATA, ICAO, name, served city, country, coordinates, region, rank, scheduled) places GeoNames places with their linked airports place_names Folded own and alternate names for place lookup admin1 First-level divisions (states, provinces) meta Key/value, including place_data_version nationalities 202 nationality → country rows for the nationality typeahead users Accounts: bcrypt hash, is_admin, is_first_login, is_active plans Saved plans: search data, selections (JSON), share token preferences Saved preferences per user recent_searches Up to 8 per user feedback Feedback widget submissions taste_signals Taste Graph signals mined from saved plans

The first six are reference data seeded from files committed to the repo; see Place and Airport Data.

docs.title: Backups (optional)
docs.text: backend/app/db/backup.py is active only when BACKUP_BUCKET is set. At startup it restores every *.db under sqlite-backups/ in the bucket. Every 60 s it uploads a snapshot, using GCS generation checks: if another instance wrote newer data, it merges that data with INSERT OR IGNORE first, and it skips uploads during a 150 s startup window. On shutdown it forces one final upload. Snapshots leave out the regenerable place tables and the place-data version, so a restored database reseeds them on start. This was built for Cloud Run's ephemeral disk; locally it is off.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text: One process-wide cachetools.TTLCache (backend/app/core/cache.py, size CACHE_MAXSIZE 500, TTL CACHE_TTL_SECONDS 1800) holds full search runs, discover and compare results (complete ones only), the /health/agents result, SerpAPI flight results and per-date calendar fares, activity and place link resolutions, Serper places data and walking-tour crawls. It does not survive a restart.

docs.title: Authentication and access
docs.text:
• POST /api/auth/login returns an HS256 JWT valid for 24 h (backend/app/core/auth.py). Passwords are bcrypt-hashed. There is no registration endpoint; admins create users.
  • Most routes require a valid token (get_current_user). Admin routes also require is_admin.
  • /api/search, /api/search/sync, /api/discover and every single-agent ("light_ai") route accept anonymous calls. They use get_optional_user: with a valid token for an active user, the Taste Graph is applied and the rate-limit key is the user; otherwise, including for a deactivated user's token, the caller is anonymous and keyed by client IP. The SPA itself requires login for every page except /share/:token.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text: backend/app/core/rate_limit.py is an in-process sliding-window limiter attached to routers as a FastAPI dependency (backend/app/main.py). Defaults per 10 minutes: search 10, chat 30, compare 30, discover 10, light_ai 60. Over the limit the API returns 429 with Retry-After and a string detail that the frontend shows as-is. Being in-process, it only works for a single backend process. See Configuration.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
• CORS from CORS_ORIGINS.
  • AnalyticsMiddleware logs every request as JSON, except /health, /docs, /openapi.json and /redoc.
  • RequestIdMiddleware propagates or creates X-Request-ID.

UI analytics events are batched by the frontend (utils/analytics.js, every 5 s or 10 events) and posted to POST /api/analytics/events, which logs them to stdout.

docs.title: Chat Assistant
docs.text: The chat (POST /api/chat, frontend/src/pages/ChatPage.jsx, backend/app/agents/chat_agent.py) is a travel advisor. It answers questions from the model's own knowledge, and it can plan a whole trip inside the conversation.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: Task Model Conversational answers and the planning narrative claude-sonnet-4-6 Intent routing, trip-parameter extraction, plan commands claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 The chat itinerary (.agents/chat-itinerary.md, ChatItineraryAgent) claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 Specialist fallbacks and refinements the specialist agents (Haiku, via BaseAgent)

docs.title: Knowledge first, specialists last
docs.text:
Topic questions ("do I need a visa for Japan?", "which area of Barcelona is best for nightlife?") are answered from the model's own knowledge and stream straight away. No agents run, and no background verification happens.

The specialist agents (visa, sim, tips, getting_around, hotels, activities, flights) run only if the model fails to answer: the stream errors, the answer is empty, or the model says it doesn't know. Only then does the chat extract trip parameters and run the matching specialists as a fallback.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
Each message goes through an ordered router in ChatAgent.stream():

Step Trigger Behaviour 0 Jailbreak or off-topic patterns Polite refusal; chat only discusses travel 1 Plan commands ("add … to my plan", "remove …", "show my plan", "clear my plan") plan_action events that the frontend applies to My Plan 1.5 A reply to a pending clarifying question (for example the origin) Resumes planning with that slot filled 2 Planning patterns ("plan a week in Lisbon…") Comprehensive planning, or a clarifying question if something essential is missing 3 A specific topic (flights, hotels, visa, SIM, tips, transport, forex…) Knowledge-only answer; specialists only on failure 3.5 A change to the trip being discussed ("make it cheaper", "add 2 days") Refinement: re-runs only the affected specialists 3.6 Knowledge patterns (culture, packing, weather, neighbourhoods…) Knowledge answer 3.7 Anything of 4 or more words not caught yet One Haiku intent-classification call, which catches soft phrasings such as "we're thinking Lisbon in October, maybe with the kids?" 4 Everything else Plan-aware conversation

docs.title: Comprehensive planning
docs.text:
A planning request streams this sequence (_run_comprehensive_planning):

  1. planning_start with the destination.
  2. trip_map: city coordinates computed in Python, so the map appears at once.
  3. itinerary_generating.
  4. comprehensive_itinerary: the day-by-day plan from the chat-itinerary agent (60 s timeout, 120 s for multi-city).
  5. Proactive warnings, checked in parallel while the itinerary builds: rainy or rough-weather days (weather agent) and major events or disruptions on the trip dates (events agent).
  6. session_context_update, suggestions (tappable follow-up chips) and planning_done.

The frontend renders this as a TripPlanView: a Leaflet map, day cards, a budget tracker, suggestion and follow-up chips, and retry actions. Items can be added to the chat's My Plan drawer, which has the same features as on the Results page.

Clarifying questions with slot memory. If only the origin is missing, the chat asks exactly that ("Which city will you be flying from?"), remembers everything else and resumes when the user answers.

section_result events (with per-section agent_status) are used only in the specialist fallback and the refinement path (_run_specialist_agents), where individual specialists run with a 45 s timeout each.

docs.title: Refinement
docs.text:
"Make it cheaper" does not re-run everything. The chat compares the changed request with the previous one and re-runs only the specialists whose inputs changed (_FIELD_AGENTS):

Changed field Re-run departure or return date flights, hotels, activities budget flights, hotels travellers flights, hotels interests activities origin flights, visa destination flights, hotels, activities, visa, sim, tips, getting_around

docs.title: Session context and history
docs.text:
The chat endpoint is stateless. The frontend sends the messages, current selections, any search results and a session_context (destination, dates, budget, travellers, a pending question) with each request, and the server returns session_context_update events. Follow-ups like "what about hotels there?" resolve against the trip being discussed, and naming a different city in the question always wins over the remembered trip.

Chat history is stored in the browser under localStorage['chat_history_<username>'], trimmed to the last 20 messages if storage is full. utils/chatHistory.js builds text stand-ins for structured turns before they are sent back to the model.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: delta (text), done, error, suggestions, session_context_update, plan_action, planning_start, trip_map, itinerary_generating, comprehensive_itinerary, planning_done, agent_status and section_result. If the server hits an exception, it still closes the stream with a fallback delta, then error and done. The frontend parses the stream in workers/chatWorker.js.

docs.title: Personalization and safety
docs.text:
For signed-in users, the saved preferences and a short Taste Graph summary (see Personalization) are added to the system prompt and to any specialist runs, so suggestions lean towards the user's demonstrated style.

The chat does not reveal its prompts, agent names or tooling, rejects jailbreak attempts and only discusses travel. It does not show verification badges.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The backend is configured through environment variables, read by pydantic-settings in backend/app/core/config.py. Variable names are the upper-case field names. Every setting has a default, so the app always starts; the ones marked needed below must be set for it to be useful.

Settings are read from the process environment and from a .env file in the working directory (env_file=".env", unknown keys ignored). For start.sh and a manual uvicorn run that is backend/.env. For Docker Compose, put the values in your shell or a root .env, which Compose uses for variable substitution (see Setup and Installation).

docs.title: Core
docs.text: Variable Default Meaning ANTHROPIC_API_KEY "" Needed. Used by every agent. Without it, every AI call fails. JWT_SECRET_KEY "" Needed. HS256 signing key for login tokens (24 h lifetime). Changing it logs everyone out. Generate one with python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))". CORS_ORIGINS ["http://localhost:5174","http://localhost:5173"] Allowed browser origins, as a JSON list. AGENTS_DIR <repo>/.agents Directory of the agent definition files. A relative path that does not exist falls back to <repo>/.agents. AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENCY 6 Global cap on concurrent Anthropic calls across all agents. CACHE_TTL_SECONDS 1800 TTL of the in-memory result cache. CACHE_MAXSIZE 500 Maximum entries in that cache.

docs.title: Storage and backup
docs.text: Variable Default Meaning DATA_DIR backend/data Directory of the single SQLite file airports.db, which holds every table (users, plans, preferences, place data and so on). Created automatically. BACKUP_BUCKET "" Google Cloud Storage bucket for SQLite backups. Empty disables backup and restore. When set, the database is restored at startup, uploaded every 60 s and uploaded once more on shutdown. Uses Application Default Credentials.

docs.title: Live data (optional)
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning SERPAPI_KEY "" SerpAPI key for live Google Flights fares, the fare calendar and Google's price insights. Empty means flights are LLM estimates and POST /api/flights/fare-calendar returns 503. GET /health reports serpapi_configured. SERPER_KEY "" Serper.dev key for Places-to-See data (Google Places) and the second tier of activity and place link resolution. Empty means Places to See is LLM-only.

Other web lookups (link enrichment for hotels and activities, the forex agent's rate searches, walking-tour city-page discovery, and identifying an unknown airport code) go through DuckDuckGo via the ddgs package and need no key.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning ADMIN_USERNAME admin Username of the seeded admin. ADMIN_PASSWORD "" Password for the seeded admin. Empty means no admin is created. Used only when that user does not exist yet; the seeded admin is not forced to change it. ADMIN_EMAIL "" Optional email for the seeded admin.

There is no self-registration: the admin creates every other user from the Admin page.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
AI-calling endpoints are rate-limited per signed-in user, or per client IP for anonymous callers, in an in-process sliding window (backend/app/core/rate_limit.py). See API Reference for the endpoints in each bucket.

Variable Default Applies to RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED true Master switch. The test suite sets it to false. RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS 600 Window length. RATE_LIMIT_SEARCH 10 /api/search, /api/search/sync RATE_LIMIT_CHAT 30 /api/chat RATE_LIMIT_COMPARE 30 /api/compare/destination RATE_LIMIT_DISCOVER 10 /api/discover RATE_LIMIT_LIGHT_AI 60 Single-agent routes, /*/filtered, /api/flights/fare-calendar, /api/stress-test, /api/layover, /api/events, /api/walking-tours

Counters live in process memory: they reset on restart and are not shared between processes or instances, so a multi-instance deployment would need a shared store. Anonymous callers are keyed by the connecting address; behind a reverse proxy all anonymous traffic shares one key unless the proxy address is replaced (for example with uvicorn --proxy-headers).

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: LOG_FORMAT is read directly with os.getenv in backend/app/main.py, not through Settings. The default, json, gives one JSON object per line (stdlib logging with a custom formatter in backend/app/core/logging_config.py). Any other value gives plain-text logs.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
The frontend reads no environment variables at build or run time.

  • Dev: Vite proxies /api and /health to http://localhost:8001 (frontend/vite.config.js).
  • Container: nginx renders frontend/nginx.conf.template with BACKEND_URL (envsubst) and proxies /api/ and /health to it. Proxy buffering is off so SSE streams, with a 120 s read timeout.

Browser storage used by the app: tp_token (login token), tp_recent_searches_open, tp_tour_done:<username>, chat_history_<username>, and the packing-list checkbox state.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
backend/.env for local development:

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
JWT_SECRET_KEY=3f0c...   # 64 hex characters
ADMIN_PASSWORD=LocalDevPassword123
# Optional
SERPAPI_KEY=
SERPER_KEY=
RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false
LOG_FORMAT=text

Values set by docker-compose.yml: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY (default change-me-in-compose), ADMIN_PASSWORD (default admin-dev-password), DATA_DIR=/data, BACKUP_BUCKET= (empty) and CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8080 for the backend, and BACKEND_URL=http://backend:8001 for the frontend.

The retained Terraform (see Deployment) sets DATA_DIR=/tmp/data, AGENTS_DIR=/app/.agents, LOG_FORMAT=json, CORS_ORIGINS, BACKUP_BUCKET, and injects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD, SERPAPI_KEY and SERPER_KEY from Secret Manager.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
# Backend
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
# create backend/.env with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD

# Frontend
cd frontend
npm install

# Optional: pre-commit hooks
make install-hooks

Run both servers with ./start.sh (backend 8001, frontend 5174) and stop them with ./stop.sh. Details: Setup and Installation.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Branch off main.
  2. Make the change with tests: backend/tests/ for Python, *.test.js(x) next to the code for the frontend.
  3. Run the checks locally with make ci from the repo root: lint (ruff and ESLint), the security scans and both test suites, mirroring CI. See Testing and CI.
  4. Push and open a pull request to main. CI (ci.yml) runs lint, security audits, both test suites with the 70% backend coverage gate, and an image build with a Trivy scan.
  5. Merging to main publishes the docs site (docs.yml). It does not deploy the app: deploy.yml is manual-only and decommissioned (see Deployment).

Merged PRs are listed in the Changelog.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Backend: ruff for lint and format (ruff check, ruff format), Python 3.12, Pydantic v2 models for request and response shapes.
  • Frontend: ESLint with the project config; import lucide icons that shadow globals (Map, Image, History…) under an alias. Tailwind utility classes; keep pure logic in src/utils/ where it can be unit-tested.
  • Comment only where the reason is not obvious from the code.
  • No error handling for cases that cannot happen, and no abstractions beyond what the task needs.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Agent prompts are config. Change agent behaviour in .agents/<name>.md (name and description frontmatter plus the prompt). The Python class builds the user prompt and parses the JSON. See Agent System for adding an agent.
  • Agents return JSON, parsed by BaseAgent._parse_json.
  • Parallel first. Independent agents run concurrently; only the itinerary and stress test depend on other results.
  • Static first. Visa, SIM, tips, getting around, forex and the emergency card have static tables; an AI failure must never replace valid static data with an error.
  • Verification from evidence only. services/verification.py must stay pure (no network or LLM calls) and must never put an error key in the verification object.
  • Place data is generated. Do not hand-edit airports.csv, places.csv.gz, admin1.csv or countries.csv; regenerate them (see Place and Airport Data). hints.json is hand-curated; add a golden-set case for every hint you add.
  • Prompts pair a city with its country ("Lisbon, Portugal"), so agents do not guess the wrong namesake.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text: The project is released under the MIT License (LICENSE). Place data contains data from GeoNames (geonames.org), CC BY 4.0, and must keep that attribution; OurAirports data is public domain.

docs.title: Current state: decommissioned
docs.text:
Travel Planner ran on Google Cloud Run until 2026-08-30, when production was decommissioned (PR #1, "chore: decommission GCP deploy pipeline"):

  • The GCP project was deleted, together with its Cloud Run services, Artifact Registry, Terraform state bucket, backup bucket and Secret Manager secrets. The old frontend and backend URLs no longer resolve.
  • .github/workflows/deploy.yml is renamed "Deploy (decommissioned)". Its push trigger was removed, so it runs only by hand (workflow_dispatch), and a run would fail because the project and secrets no longer exist.
  • infrastructure/ (bootstrap scripts and Terraform) is kept unchanged for reference.
  • The backend still contains the GCS backup code (backend/app/db/backup.py); it does nothing unless BACKUP_BUCKET is set.

There is no hosted instance. To use the app, run it locally (see Setup and Installation):

./start.sh                       # dev servers on :8001 and :5174
# or
docker compose up --build        # containers on :8001 and :8080

The documentation site (https://rupakc.github.io/travel-planner/) is separate and still published by docs.yml; see Testing and CI.

docs.title: What the retained setup deploys
docs.text:
Piece Where Backend image backend/Dockerfile (python:3.12-slim, built from the repo root; copies backend/ and .agents/; uvicorn on 8001, 1 worker) Frontend image frontend/Dockerfile (node:20-alpine build, nginx:alpine on 8080; BACKEND_URL templated into nginx.conf.template) Cloud Run backend travel-planner-backend, 2 vCPU / 2 GiB, min = max = 1 instance (the SQLite file and the in-process rate limiter assume a single process) Cloud Run frontend travel-planner-frontend, 1 vCPU / 512 MiB, 0–3 instances Storage <project>-sqlite-backup bucket for SQLite snapshots; <project>-tf-state for Terraform state Secrets Secret Manager: anthropic-api-key, jwt-secret-key, admin-password, serpapi-key, serper-key Other modules Artifact Registry, IAM, monitoring (uptime check on /health, alert policies, log metrics, dashboard), project APIs

Terraform lives in infrastructure/terraform/ (modules artifact_registry, backend_service, frontend_service, iam, monitoring, project, secrets, storage). The backend service sets DATA_DIR=/tmp/data, AGENTS_DIR=/app/.agents, LOG_FORMAT=json, BACKUP_BUCKET and CORS_ORIGINS (the frontend URL), and injects the secrets as environment variables.

Cloud Run's disk is ephemeral, which is why backups exist: on start the backend restores the database from the bucket, uploads a snapshot every 60 s and uploads once more on shutdown (see Architecture).

docs.title: Redeploying to GCP
docs.text: A redeploy creates a new project; nothing from the old one can be recovered from GCP. These steps follow the retained scripts and workflow; they have not been run since the decommissioning, so expect to fix drift (provider versions, API changes).

docs.title: 1. Bootstrap the project
docs.text:
You need the gcloud CLI, authenticated, and a billing account.

BILLING_ACCOUNT=XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX bash infrastructure/scripts/bootstrap.sh
# optional: PROJECT_NAME=travel-planner REGION=europe-west1

bootstrap.sh creates the project <PROJECT_NAME>-prod, links billing, enables the Cloud Run, Artifact Registry, Secret Manager, Storage, IAM, Resource Manager, Compute, Monitoring and Logging APIs, creates the versioned <project>-tf-state bucket, and creates a github-actions-sa service account with deploy roles. It writes a key file, github-sa-key.json, to the current directory. Keep it out of git and delete it once it is stored as a secret.

docs.title: 2. Add the GitHub repository secrets
docs.text:
Secret Value GCP_PROJECT_ID The new project ID (<PROJECT_NAME>-prod) GCP_SA_KEY Contents of github-sa-key.json ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Anthropic key JWT_SECRET_KEY A random secret, for example openssl rand -hex 32 ADMIN_PASSWORD Password for the seeded admin SERPAPI_KEY SerpAPI key (live flights, fare calendar) SERPER_KEY Serper key (Places to See, link resolution)

The workflow's bootstrap job copies the last five into Secret Manager. (infrastructure/scripts/populate-secrets.sh does the same interactively, after Terraform has created the secret shells; you need one or the other, not both.) bootstrap.sh also prints TF_STATE_BUCKET and GCP_BILLING_ACCOUNT; the current workflow derives the state bucket from the project ID and does not read either.

Also check the terraform job's environment in deploy.yml: TF_VAR_admin_email is hard-coded and receives monitoring alerts. See infrastructure/terraform/terraform.tfvars.example for the Terraform variables (project_id, region, admin_email, backend_image, frontend_image, frontend_url).

docs.title: 3. Re-enable and run the workflow
docs.text:
Edit .github/workflows/deploy.yml: remove the DECOMMISSIONED banner, rename it, and, if you want automatic deploys again, restore the trigger:

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

Then run it from the Actions tab (or push to main). Its three jobs:

  1. bootstrap: enables the APIs, creates the Terraform state bucket and the travel-planner Artifact Registry repository if missing, and upserts the Secret Manager secrets from the GitHub secrets.
  2. push-images: builds both images with Buildx (docker buildx build -f backend/Dockerfile . and frontend/), tagged with the commit SHA and latest, and pushes them to europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/<project>/travel-planner.
  3. terraform: init against the state bucket, validate, imports resources that exist in GCP but not in state, reads the frontend URL for CORS_ORIGINS, then plan and apply, and prints both service URLs.

On the very first apply the frontend does not exist yet, so CORS falls back to localhost; run the workflow a second time to pick up the frontend URL.

docs.title: 4. After the first deploy
docs.text:
• Sign in as admin with ADMIN_PASSWORD and create users from the Admin page; there is no self-registration.
  • Check GET /health and GET /health/agents on the backend URL.
  • The place data seeds itself on the first start (about 2 s). Backups leave the place tables out, so every restore reseeds them.

docs.title: Deploying elsewhere
docs.text:
Any host that can run the two containers works. Requirements:

  • One backend process (rate limits and the SQLite file are per-process), with a persistent volume for DATA_DIR, or BACKUP_BUCKET and GCS credentials if the disk is ephemeral.
  • ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY and ADMIN_PASSWORD set; SERPAPI_KEY and SERPER_KEY optional.
  • CORS_ORIGINS set to the frontend's origin, and BACKEND_URL for the frontend container.
  • If the backend sits behind a proxy, run uvicorn with --proxy-headers so anonymous rate limits key on real client IPs.

docker-compose.yml is a working single-host example (see Setup and Installation).

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text: A React 18 single-page app built with Vite 6, React Router 6 (react-router-dom 6.28) and Tailwind CSS 3.4. Maps use Leaflet with react-leaflet, icons come from lucide-react, and HTTP goes through axios. @tanstack/react-query provides a QueryClientProvider in main.jsx. What the user sees is described in Trip Planning Features; this page covers how the code is organised.

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
frontend/src/
├── main.jsx                  QueryClientProvider, BrowserRouter, AuthProvider
├── App.jsx                   routes, auth guards, always-mounted tabs, footer
├── index.css                 Tailwind directives
├── pages/
│   ├── SearchPage.jsx        known / surprise-me / compare modes, recent searches, tour
│   ├── ResultsPage.jsx       streamed sections, planning tools, My Plan drawer (~4,300 lines)
│   ├── ChatPage.jsx          chat, TripPlanView, chat plan drawer
│   ├── PreferencesPage.jsx   preferences + Taste Graph card
│   ├── AdminPage.jsx         users and feedback (admins only)
│   ├── LoginPage.jsx
│   ├── ChangePasswordPage.jsx
│   └── SharePage.jsx         public read-only shared plan, PNG download
├── components/
│   ├── BestValuePackage, BudgetPlanner, CompareTable, CostBreakdown,
│   │   FareCalendarStrip (+ PriceInsightsChip), FeedbackWidget, ItinerarySection,
│   │   OnboardingTour, PlanExport, PlanViewModal, RecentSearches, TimelineView,
│   │   TripMap, VerificationBadge, WalkingToursSection
│   └── ui/                   AirportSearch, NationalitySearch, NavBar, TagInput,
│                             TravelerPanel, AttributionFooter
├── context/
│   ├── AuthContext.jsx       token, user, preferences and two-way sync
│   └── SearchDataContext.jsx search form and results state
├── hooks/useFirstRunTour.js  when to show the onboarding tour
├── services/api.js           axios client and API helpers
├── utils/                    pure helpers (see below)
└── workers/
    ├── sseWorker.js          parses the /api/search stream
    └── chatWorker.js         parses the /api/chat stream

Tests sit next to the code as *.test.js(x) (vitest + jsdom); see Testing and CI.

docs.title: Routing and always-mounted tabs
docs.text:
Routes in App.jsx:

Path Page Access /login LoginPage Public /share/:token SharePage Public /change-password ChangePasswordPage Signed in / SearchPage, then ResultsPage Signed in /chat ChatPage Signed in /preferences PreferencesPage Signed in /admin AdminPage Admins (RequireAdmin) anything else redirect to /

Search/Results and Chat are always mounted and hidden with CSS, so navigating away never loses streaming results, a half-typed message or a response in progress. Preferences and Admin mount on each visit. SearchDataProvider sits inside the signed-in Layout, so logging out discards all search state. A user flagged requires_password_change is redirected to /change-password. AttributionFooter renders the GeoNames and OurAirports credit under every page. Each route change sends a page-view analytics event.

docs.title: State
docs.text:
• AuthContext keeps the JWT (localStorage['tp_token']), the user (username, is_admin, requires_password_change) and the saved preferences. It loads preferences after login and writes Search-form values back to them on submit (the two-way binding).
  • SearchDataContext holds the search form, the streamed results and per-agent status, shared by SearchPage and ResultsPage.
  • Plan selections, itinerary overlays and planner settings are local state in ResultsPage and ChatPage.

docs.title: Streaming workers
docs.text: sseWorker.js POSTs to /api/search, reads the body as a stream, splits data: events, and posts each parsed event to the main thread, which only updates React state. If the stream closes without a done event it posts __interrupted. chatWorker.js does the same for /api/chat. Keeping the parsing off the main thread keeps the UI responsive while large payloads arrive.

docs.title: API layer
docs.text: services/api.js is an axios instance that adds Authorization: Bearer <token>, plus helpers: streamSearch (spawns the worker), the filtered searches, fetchFareCalendar, getSerpapiConfigured (reads /health once per page load), discoverDestinations, the recent-search calls, compareDestination and recheckStressTest. utils/httpError.js turns error responses into messages, showing a string detail (such as the 429 rate-limit message) as-is.

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text:
Pure, unit-tested helpers in src/utils/:

Module Purpose analytics.js Batches UI events and posts them to /api/analytics/events (every 5 s or 10 events) bestValuePackage.js Rule-based best-value picks budgetPlanner.js Budget split and fit checks chatHistory.js Text stand-ins for structured chat turns compare.js Compare-mode requests and table model fareCalendar.js Fare-calendar cells and date shifting geo.js Great-circle distance (haversineKm) httpError.js Error messages from API responses itineraryLayout.js Drag-and-drop overlay (arrangeItinerary, fingerprints) orderSectionByCity.js Stable sort of multi-city lists into journey order planExport.js .ics export planHelpers.js Plan cost, cost breakdown, names, counts planPrint.js Print/PDF page recentSearches.js Recent-search formatting and date roll-forward remix.js Trip Remix presets schedule.js Estimated start/end times (scheduleDays) stressTestPayload.js Payload for the health-check re-check tour.js Onboarding-tour completion flag verification.js Resolving pending badges, stripping link evidence from saved plans

docs.title: Maps
docs.text: TripMap.jsx renders the itinerary with Leaflet and OpenStreetMap tiles: numbered markers per activity stop, a dashed polyline in visit order, popups, and fitBounds on the activity area. The chat page draws its own map in the same style for city markers and place pins, and leaves the origin out of the bounds so the view does not zoom out across continents.

docs.title: Dev server and production build
docs.text:
• npm run dev starts Vite on port 5174. vite.config.js proxies /api and /health to http://localhost:8001.
  • npm run build writes dist/. The container (frontend/Dockerfile) builds with node:20-alpine and serves dist/ from nginx:alpine on port 8080. nginx.conf.template proxies /api/ and /health to BACKEND_URL, with buffering off for SSE and a 120 s read timeout.
  • The app uses no VITE_* environment variables.

docs.title: Travel Planner — Developer Docs
docs.text:
Travel Planner turns a route, travel dates, a budget and a list of interests into a complete trip plan. A team of Claude agents builds the plan, and the results stream to the browser section by section as each agent finishes.

These pages are the technical documentation for people working on the code. The project is open source under the MIT License (LICENSE at the repo root).

No hosted instance. The production deployment on Google Cloud Run was decommissioned on 2026-08-30: the GCP project was deleted and the old app URLs no longer work. To try the app, run it locally with ./start.sh or docker compose up --build (see Setup and Installation). Deployment explains how to bring a hosted copy back.

docs.title: What the app does
docs.text:
• Search in three modes: I know where I'm going (one city or up to 3 stops on the way), Surprise me (5 suggested destinations), and Compare (2–3 destinations side by side). Recent searches are kept per user.
  • Results: 16 sections (flights, weather, hotels, activities, places to see, free walking tours, events, visa, SIM, tips, emergency card, getting around, forex, itinerary, trip health check and packing list), each with a source-verification label.
  • Planning tools on the Results page: a best-value package, a client-side budget planner, an opt-in fare calendar with Google Flights price insights, Trip Remix presets, and an itinerary you can rearrange by drag-and-drop with estimated times, edits, notes and a re-check.
  • My Plan drawer: pick items into a plan, see the cost breakdown, export to calendar (.ics) or print/PDF, save plans and share them by public link.
  • Chat: a travel advisor that answers from model knowledge and can plan a whole trip in the conversation.
  • Personalization: saved preferences bound two ways to the Search form, and a Taste Graph learned from saved plans.
  • Accounts: admin-created users (no self-registration), an admin page, a feedback widget and per-user rate limits.

Trip Planning Features describes each of these in detail.

docs.title: How a search works, in brief
docs.text:
1. Phase 0 (instant). Static lookup tables yield visa, SIM, tips, getting-around and forex results, the Travel Ease confidence grade and the emergency card, all marked source: "static".
  2. Phase 1 (parallel AI). Thirteen specialist agents run concurrently and stream their results as they finish. For the six static-backed agents (visa, sim, tips, getting_around, forex, emergency_card) an AI failure is suppressed, so the static data stays on screen. Two deferred agents, packing list and pricing advisor, start as soon as their inputs are ready.
  3. Phase 2. The itinerary agent starts once activities and hotels are in (60 s timeout, template fallback). When the itinerary is final, the stress-test agent audits it.

Every specialist agent uses Claude Haiku 4.5 through BaseAgent. Chat uses Claude Sonnet 4.6 for conversational answers. See Architecture and Agent System.
