Place data contains data from GeoNames (geonames.org), CC BY 4.0. Airport data comes from OurAirports (public domain). See Place and Airport Data.

docs.title: Multi-City Trips
docs.text: Travel Planner supports full multi-stop journeys — e.g. New York → Paris → Rome → Barcelona → New York — with every section of the results page covering every stop, in the exact order you entered them.

docs.title: Requesting a multi-city trip
docs.text:
The "To" city is the final destination; any added stops are intermediate cities visited on the way there. The destinations list is the full journey in travel order — stops first, final destination last — and destination is that final city:

{
  "origin": "NYC",
  "destination": "Barcelona",
  "destinations": ["Paris", "Rome", "Barcelona"],
  "departure_date": "2026-09-10",
  "return_date": "2026-09-19",
  "destination_nights": [2, 3, null],
  "nationality": "American"
}

destination_nights is optional and aligned with destinations: set exact nights for any stop and leave the rest null — unspecified cities (typically the final destination) share the remaining days automatically.

On the Search page, enter your final destination in To, then add up to 3 stops in the order you'll pass through them (4 cities in all); each stop has an optional nights field (1–30).

Single-city only: the fare calendar, Google's price insights and Compare mode work only for single-destination trips. POST /api/flights/fare-calendar and POST /api/compare/destination answer multi-city requests with 422.

docs.title: How days are allocated — city_stays
docs.text:
Cities with explicit destination_nights get exactly those days; the remaining days are split proportionally across the rest (TravelSearchRequest.city_stays in backend/app/schemas/request.py). With no nights specified, an N-city trip of D days uses round(i × D / N) boundaries so every date is covered exactly once regardless of how unevenly the division falls:

City Start End (move-on day) Nights Paris Sep 10 Sep 13 3 Rome Sep 13 Sep 16 3 Barcelona Sep 16 Sep 19 3

Each stay's end_date is the day the traveler moves on — it equals the next city's start_date, and the last city's end is the return date.

docs.title: Flights — one search per leg
docs.text:
flight_legs decomposes the journey into one-way legs: origin → city₁ on the departure date, an inter-city hop on each move-on day, and last city → origin on the return date.

The flights pipeline (backend/app/services/serp_flights.py::search_multi_city) then:

  1. Resolves every endpoint to up to 3 scheduled airport codes with lookup_city_iata (local database only; see Place and Airport Data). A city that is ambiguous, such as "Valencia" without a country, resolves to nothing, and that leg falls back to an AI estimate.
  2. Fires parallel one-way Google Flights searches (SerpAPI, type: "2") — one per leg, with a 20 s timeout and one retry per leg.
  3. Tags every result with leg_index, leg_from, leg_to, leg_date, and city, keeps the top 5 per leg, and sorts legs into the user's journey order before returning.
  4. Any leg SerpAPI cannot serve (timeout, zero results) is AI-filled with realistic estimates (FlightsAgent._ai_fill_legs, marked source: "estimate"), so no leg ever shows an empty row.

If SerpAPI is unavailable entirely, the AI agent produces all legs from a prompt that lists each leg explicitly and demands leg_index per result; FlightsAgent._group_legs regroups the flat output into ordered legs.

The UI renders one group per leg ("Leg 1 · NYC → Paris · Sep 10") and lets you pick one flight per leg, with a running total for the chosen combination.

docs.title: Every section covers every stop
docs.text:
Specialist prompts carry a mandatory coverage block with per-city quotas so no stop is skipped:

Section Per-city quota Places to See 4–6 (with per-city Serper search context) Walking Tours each city crawled separately, topped up to ≥ min(4, available) Activities ≥ 5 Hotels ≥ 3 What's On (events) 2–4 Getting Around intra-city options per city + inter-city hops (train/bus/flight)

Every result carries a city field, rendered as a 📍 city chip on each card so items are easy to attribute at a glance.

docs.title: Journey order is guaranteed, twice
docs.text:
LLM output order is not trusted:

  • Backend — flight legs are sorted by leg_index; weather days are sorted by (stay order, date).
  • Frontend — orderSectionByCity (frontend/src/utils/orderSectionByCity.js) stable-sorts every city-tagged section list by the index of its city in your entered stop order, the moment results arrive.

The itinerary agent is instructed to visit cities in exactly the order requested — it never reorders your route.

docs.title: Weather per stay
docs.text:
WeatherAgent forecasts each city only for the dates you are actually there:

  • Trips starting within 16 days use the Open-Meteo forecast per stay (free, no key needed).
  • Further-out trips fall back to one LLM climate-estimate call covering all stays. The parser tolerates the model nesting output per city (_flatten_days), assigns each day's city authoritatively from the stay date ranges, dedupes hand-over dates, and sorts by stop order.

The UI groups day cards under a 📍 header per city, in journey order.

docs.title: Visas across countries
docs.text: For multi-country routes the visa agent evaluates entry requirements for every country on the itinerary against your nationality, residence permits, and existing visas — not just the first stop.

docs.title: Personalization
docs.text: Three layers tune results to the traveller: saved preferences, per-search settings, and the learned Taste Graph.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text:
Saved per account (GET/PUT /api/preferences, frontend/src/pages/PreferencesPage.jsx):

  • Travel Budget: Budget, Mid-range or Luxury (pre-fills the Search budget as 1000, 3000 or 8000 USD).
  • Identity: nationality and current residence (used as the default departure city).
  • Documents: residence permits and existing visas.
  • Travel Style: interests, the traveller mix and accessibility needs.

Two-way binding (frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx): saved preferences pre-fill the Search form on load, and submitting a search writes its fields back to preferences. The app therefore always remembers the latest defaults. A loaded recent search takes precedence over the pre-fill.

docs.title: Recent searches
docs.text: Every submitted search, from the Search form or from the Results page's search panel, is saved to the account (/api/recent-searches): the newest 8, with identical searches merged (interest order ignored). They appear in a collapsible strip above the Search form; see Trip Planning Features.

docs.title: Per-search settings
docs.text:
These are fields of TravelSearchRequest (backend/app/schemas/request.py) that agents receive in their prompts:

  • Serendipity (serendipity, 0.0–1.0), the Search form's "Discovery style" slider: Famous classics, Balanced mix, Hidden gems. At the hidden-gems end, agents prefer local favourites and mark results hidden_gem: true.
  • Pace (pace: relaxed, balanced or packed) controls how densely the itinerary fills each day. It has no control on the Search form: the "Slow it down" remix sets it to relaxed, and API callers can set it directly.
  • Traveller mix: adults (18–64), seniors (65+), children (5–17), infants (0–4). It shapes fare notes, hotel suitability and activity choices.
  • Accessibility needs: wheelchair, visual, hearing, cognitive. They are passed into every agent prompt.
  • Interests: activities get a model-assigned relevance score (0.0–1.0) and are sorted by it.

docs.title: Taste Graph
docs.text:
The Taste Graph (backend/app/db/taste_db.py) learns a user's style from what they save into plans, with no forms to fill.

  1. Saving a plan (POST/PUT /api/plans) mines its selections for signals (extract_signals): flight style (non-stop or cheapest, per selected leg), hotel tier and type, activity categories and budget band. They are stored in the taste_signals table.
  2. derive_taste_context() condenses the signals into a short sentence, for example "Prefers non-stop flights, mid-range boutique hotels, food and history activities."
  3. On /api/search (with a valid token), /api/chat and their specialist runs, the server sets TravelSearchRequest.taste_context from the user's profile; a value sent by the client is ignored.

Agents use it to rank matching options higher, never to filter options out, so all budget tiers still appear. Because taste_context is part of the search cache key, cached results are per profile and never leak between users.

The Preferences page shows what has been learned (GET /api/taste-profile) and has a Reset button (DELETE /api/taste-profile).

docs.title: Place and Airport Data
docs.text: Travel Planner turns whatever the user types ("Milano", "Portland, ME", "Zermatt") into airport codes for live flight search, and offers an airport-and-place typeahead. Both run against open data committed to the repo and seeded into SQLite. No web call is involved, except for one narrow case described under Bare airport codes.

docs.title: Sources and licences
docs.text:
Source Files used Licence OurAirports airports.csv, regions.csv, countries.csv Public domain GeoNames cities1000.txt, admin1CodesASCII.txt CC BY 4.0

Attribution: Contains data from GeoNames (geonames.org), CC BY 4.0. The GeoNames data has been modified (filtered, name-folded, scored and linked to airports), and GeoNames does not endorse these changes. Airport data comes from OurAirports.

The app footer shows "Place data © GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) · Airport data: OurAirports". backend/app/db/data/README.md holds the full source, licence and derivation notes.

Snapshot date of both sources: 2026-10-29.

docs.title: Committed files
docs.text:
backend/app/db/data/:

File Size Contents airports.csv 347 KB 4,014 airports (4,010 with scheduled service): iata, icao, name, city, country, country_code, region, type_rank, scheduled, lat, lng places.csv.gz 5.5 MB 162,014 GeoNames places with at least 1,000 people (excluding sections of places and historical, abandoned or destroyed places), each linked to up to 3 ranked airports, with folded alternate names for places of 15k or more admin1.csv 121 KB 3,865 first-level divisions (states, provinces, regions) countries.csv 3.5 KB Every OurAirports country, used for country names in resolution hints.json 15 KB Hand-curated, not generated (see below) README.md 10 KB Sources, licences, derivation rules, regeneration, conflict report

The total is about 6 MB (the limit is 8 MB). In addition, backend/app/db/seed_airports.py holds a curated list of 402 airports with served-city overrides, and REPLACED_CODES maps 14 retired codes to their replacements (for example PNH → KTI).

docs.title: hints.json
docs.text:
Curated knowledge the open data lacks:

Key Entries Purpose islands 104 Islands and their airports ("Sicily" → CTA, PMO, TPS) destinations 82 Places without a useful airport of their own ("Machu Picchu" → CUZ, "Kyoto" → KIX, ITM; "Zermatt" → ZRH, GVA; "Monte Carlo" → NCE) regions 20 Regions ("Algarve" → FAO) exonyms 80 Other-language or English names mapped to a GeoNames id, or to "ambiguous" ("Cologne" → Köln, "Milano" → Milan; "Odessa" is ambiguous unless qualified) city_aliases 19 Shorthands (SF, LA, KL, HCMC, NOLA…) country_aliases 43 "UK", "England", "Holland"… saint_exceptions 2 Names that must not get St/Saint variants

docs.title: Regenerating the data
docs.text:
backend/scripts/build_place_data.py is standard-library only and deterministic (sorted rows, gzip mtime 0); it takes about 5 s and treats the downloaded sources as untrusted input. Download the OurAirports CSVs and GeoNames cities1000.zip / admin1CodesASCII.txt into a directory of their own, then from the repo root:

python3 -I backend/scripts/build_place_data.py \
    --ourairports /path/to/ourairports-src \
    --geonames-cities /path/to/geonames-src/extracted/cities1000.txt \
    --geonames-admin1 /path/to/geonames-src/admin1CodesASCII.txt \
    --out backend/app/db/data > conflicts.txt

The script writes airports.csv, places.csv.gz, admin1.csv and countries.csv, and prints a summary and a conflict report to stdout (not committed). Then run python3 -m pytest tests/test_build_place_data.py from backend/, update the snapshot date in the data README, and commit the four files. hints.json is edited by hand.

docs.title: Versioned seeding
docs.text:
At startup, seed() in backend/app/db/seed_airports.py loads the files into the airports, places, place_names and admin1 tables of $DATA_DIR/airports.db.

  • The data version is the sha256 of a loader tag plus the bytes of airports.csv, places.csv.gz and admin1.csv, truncated to 16 hex characters and stored as meta.place_data_version.
  • If the stored version matches, seeding is skipped (about 5 ms).
  • Otherwise one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (waiting up to 30 s for another worker's lock) upserts the airports, sets scheduled = 0 on old rows missing from the dataset, and rebuilds places, place names and divisions with their indexes. On an empty database this takes about 2 s and produces about 316,000 name rows and a database of about 29 MB.
  • Backups leave these tables and the version out, so a restored database reseeds them.

It can also be run by hand: cd backend && python -m app.db.seed_airports. After seeding, places_db.warm() builds an in-memory airport-name index (about 0.06 s).

docs.title: How a typed place resolves
docs.text: lookup_city_iata(text) (backend/app/db/database.py) returns up to 3 comma-joined scheduled airport codes, best first, or None. The request validator (backend/app/schemas/request.py) uses it to fill origin_iata and destination_iata for flight search, the fare calendar and Compare. When it returns None, flights fall back to AI estimates for that route.

docs.title: The rules, in order
docs.text:
1. An airport code. An upper-case three-letter code is used as typed, after mapping retired codes ("LHR" → LHR, "PNH" → KTI). Lower-case text tries places first and falls back to the code only if it is a scheduled airport ("lhr" → LHR).
  2. A typeahead label such as "LGW — London, United Kingdom" uses its code alone.
  3. A curated hint: an island, destination or region from hints.json, unless a stated country contradicts it.
  4. The curated city list: airports whose served city matches the text (accent-folded, with St/Saint variants and city aliases), restricted by any stated country, ISO code, alias or region code. A city name that is ambiguous or contested gives None.
  5. GeoNames place resolution (resolve_place, backend/app/db/places_db.py):
  6. Candidates are places whose own name matches. Alternate names count only when no place has that own name, or when the own-name places are small (under 20k) and the alternate one is at least 10× bigger and 150k or more.
  7. Exonyms from hints.json map an English name to a specific place, or mark it ambiguous.
  8. A country typed alone gives its top place; a first-level division ("Florida", "Scotland") joins as its top place unless a town of that name is comparably notable.
  9. Stated qualifiers (country, ISO code, alias, US/CA/AU/BR/IN region code or a division name) filter the candidates. A qualifier that contradicts every candidate gives None.
  10. An airport whose whole name equals the text can win ("Wagga Wagga" → WGA), but never over a place of 40k or more.
  11. The winner must score 3× the next candidate (score = population × notability). A place under 15k wins only alone or through a hint; one under 5k with no airport within 100 km gives None.
  12. The place's linked airports are returned. With a curated city in the same country they are appended to the curated codes ("New York" → JFK, LGA, EWR); otherwise foreign airports are dropped unless the place has no domestic one.
  13. Last resort: dataset airports whose display city matches.

Text without a comma is also tried as "City, Qualifier" when the last words name a country or region ("Chicago IL", "Berlin Germany"). Generic affixes are retried too ("Zanzibar Island", "Banff National Park", "Tokyo city").

docs.title: Bare airport codes
docs.text: The one web path: when a request's origin or destination is a bare 3-letter code that is not in the database or REPLACED_CODES, lookup_iata runs a DuckDuckGo search plus a Haiku extraction to name the city, and stores the answer (backend/app/db/database.py). Everything else is local.

docs.title: Folding and shared rules
docs.text: app.core.places.fold_place (accent and case folding) is shared by the generator and the runtime, so names match the same way in both. backend/app/core/places.py also loads hints.json and defines OWN_AIRPORT_KM = 25 and NEVER_LINK = {"ECN"} (Ercan is never suggested for a place, only when typed). Region code tables for the US, Canada, Australia, Brazil and India live in backend/app/db/airport_regions.py.

docs.title: Autocomplete
docs.text:
GET /api/airports/search?q=&limit= (search_airports in backend/app/db/database.py; default 10 results, at most 50):

  • Matches airports by code, city, airport name or country, plus the airports of GeoNames places and curated hints whose folded name starts with the query ("kyoto" → ITM, KIX, …; "milan" → MXP, LIN, BGY).
  • Alternate names count for places of 100k or more from the fourth letter ("münch" → München).
  • A place contributes only its own-country airports, and only places scoring at least 1/10 of the best match count.
  • Order: exact code, code prefix, exact name, name prefix, then the rest. Lower-case three-letter text that names a place lists the place first ("hue" → HUI; "HUE" → HUE). Within a class, the more notable place comes first, then curated order, then the bigger airport.
  • "Contains" matches are dropped once there are real matches, and unscheduled airports appear only for their exact code.

Each row has iata_code, name, city, country, country_code.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• Golden set. backend/tests/data/golden_places.csv has 693 cases (400 resolution, 275 data, 18 autocomplete; 541 "first code matches", 94 exact, 50 subset and 8 expected None). tests/test_golden_places_runtime.py runs them all and forbids web calls.
  • Fresh blind probe. On inputs not used during development, about 1.7% resolved to a wrong airport. More inputs now resolve to None by design: when a name is genuinely ambiguous, no answer (and an AI-estimated fare) is better than a confident wrong airport.
  • Speed. lookup_city_iata takes well under 2 ms per call (p50 about 0.6 ms), so request handlers call it synchronously.

docs.title: Setup and Installation
docs.text: How to run Travel Planner on your own machine. There is no hosted instance any more (see Deployment), so this is also how to try the app.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 (the Dockerfile and CI use 3.12; pyproject.toml allows 3.11 or later).
  • Node.js 20 (the Dockerfile and CI use 20; vitest 4 needs ^20 || ^22 || >=24 and jsdom 27 needs 20 or later).
  • An Anthropic API key. Every agent calls Claude. Without a key the app starts, but every AI section fails.
  • Docker with Compose, only for the container setup.
  • Optional: a SerpAPI key (SERPAPI_KEY) for live Google Flights fares, the fare calendar and price insights, and a Serper key (SERPER_KEY) for Places-to-See data and link resolution. Without them, flights come from the LLM and the fare calendar is hidden.

docs.title: Option A: start.sh (recommended for development)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rupakc/travel-planner.git
cd travel-planner

# Backend dependencies (a virtualenv is recommended)
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt          # add -r requirements-dev.txt for tests and linters
cd ..

Create backend/.env. The backend reads .env from its working directory, which is backend/ when started by start.sh:

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
JWT_SECRET_KEY=<output of: python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))">
ADMIN_PASSWORD=<a password for the seeded admin account>
# Optional
SERPAPI_KEY=
SERPER_KEY=

Then, from the repo root:

./start.sh              # backend on :8001, frontend on :5174
./start.sh --backend    # just one side
./start.sh --frontend
./stop.sh               # stop both (--backend, --frontend, --force)

start.sh runs uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8001 from backend/ and npm run dev (Vite on port 5174) from frontend/. It runs npm install when node_modules is missing, warns when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or backend/.env is missing, waits up to 30 s for each port, writes PIDs to .pids/ and logs to .logs/backend.log and .logs/frontend.log. stop.sh gives each process a 10 s grace period; --force sends SIGKILL.

Open http://localhost:5174. The API's Swagger UI is at http://localhost:8001/docs.

docs.title: Option B: by hand
docs.text:
# Terminal 1
cd backend && pip install -r requirements.txt && uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001 --reload

# Terminal 2
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev

The Vite dev server proxies /api and /health to http://localhost:8001 (frontend/vite.config.js). The frontend has no .env and reads no VITE_* variables.

docs.title: Option C: Docker Compose
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rupakc/travel-planner.git
cd travel-planner
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...   # or put it in a .env file at the repo root
docker compose up --build
  • Frontend (nginx): http://localhost:8080
  • Backend: http://localhost:8001 (Swagger UI at /docs)

docker-compose.yml builds the backend from the repo root (context: ., dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile), because the image copies both backend/ and .agents/. Compose reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY and ADMIN_PASSWORD from your shell or a root .env. If unset, JWT_SECRET_KEY falls back to change-me-in-compose and ADMIN_PASSWORD to admin-dev-password; change both for anything other than a local trial. The backend stores its database in the backend_data volume (DATA_DIR=/data), GCS backup is off, and the frontend waits for the backend's /health check. docker compose down -v also deletes the volume and therefore all users and plans.

docs.title: What happens on first start
docs.text:
The backend's startup (backend/app/main.py, lifespan) runs in this order:

  1. Restore from GCS (only when BACKUP_BUCKET is set).
  2. Seed the place and airport data into $DATA_DIR/airports.db. This takes about 2 s on the first start and about 5 ms afterwards, because the seed is versioned (see Place and Airport Data).
  3. Build the in-memory airport-name index (about 0.06 s).
  4. Seed the nationalities and create the remaining tables.
  5. Seed the admin account, if ADMIN_PASSWORD is set.
  6. Start the 60 s backup loop (a no-op without BACKUP_BUCKET).

All data lives in one SQLite file, $DATA_DIR/airports.db. DATA_DIR defaults to backend/data, which is gitignored.

docs.title: First login
docs.text:
There is no self-registration. Accounts are created by an admin.

  1. Open the app and sign in as admin (or your ADMIN_USERNAME) with the ADMIN_PASSWORD you set. The seeded admin is not asked to change the password.
  2. Open the Admin tab and create users with a temporary password (at least 8 characters). Those users must change it on first login.

ADMIN_PASSWORD is only used to create the admin account when it does not exist yet. Changing it later does not change an existing admin's password.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
cd backend && python3 -m pytest -q
cd frontend && npm test

See Testing and CI for coverage, lint and the Node 20.18 workaround.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Every AI section shows an error. The Anthropic key is missing or invalid, or the account is out of quota. Check .logs/backend.log. GET /health/agents makes one tiny Haiku call and reports whether the LLM is reachable.

"Network Error" in the browser. The backend is not running on port 8001, which the Vite proxy expects.

No fare calendar and only estimated fares. SERPAPI_KEY is not set. GET /health reports serpapi_configured.

429 "Too many requests". You hit a rate limit (for example 10 searches per 10 minutes). Raise the RATE_LIMIT_* values or set RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false for local work (see Configuration).

Port already in use. Run ./stop.sh --force, or change the host port mappings in docker-compose.yml.

Log lines are JSON. That is the default. Set LOG_FORMAT to any value other than json for plain-text logs.

docs.title: Sharing and Plans
docs.text: The My Plan drawer, saved plans, export and public share links.

docs.title: My Plan drawer
docs.text:
Both the Results page and Chat page carry a plan drawer. Anything in the results can be selected into it:

  • Flights: one per leg on multi-city trips (selections.flights is an array keyed by leg_index); a single round-trip selection otherwise
  • Hotel, activities, places to see, free walking tours (selections.walking_tours, keyed by url), events, SIM plan, tips, transport options and packing-list items
  • Itinerary slots: individual morning, afternoon or evening activities. A picked slot keeps its estimated start and end times, so My Plan, saved and shared plans show, for example, "Day 2 · Afternoon · 13:30–16:00".

Alongside the picks, a plan stores an itinerary snapshot and the itinerary overlays: itinerary_layout (drag-and-drop moves and removals), itinerary_edits (edited activity, location or cost) and itinerary_notes. See Trip Planning Features.

The drawer shows a live cost total (computePlanCost sums flight legs, hotel nights, and per-person activity prices) and supports drag-and-drop from result cards.

Under the plan name, Where the money goes (components/CostBreakdown.jsx) breaks that total down by category — flights, hotel, activities, SIM — as a stacked bar plus one row per category with its amount and share, biggest first. The rows come from computePlanCostBreakdown() and computePlanCost() is defined as their sum, so the parts always add up to the total. Local transport only carries free-text fares, so it's left out and the drawer says so when transport options are selected.

docs.title: Export: calendar and print/PDF
docs.text:
The My Plan drawer (Results and Chat) and the saved-plan viewer have two export buttons (components/PlanExport.jsx):

  • Add to calendar downloads an .ics file (buildPlanIcs in frontend/src/utils/planExport.js) that Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook can import. It holds one event per itinerary activity at its estimated start and end time (the same derived schedule the Results page shows, scheduleDays in utils/schedule.js, applied to the arranged itinerary), with your slot edits and notes. Picks from plans saved before timed itineraries fall back to fixed slot hours (morning 09:00–12:00, afternoon 13:00–17:00, evening 18:00–21:00). Flights are timed events from their departure time and duration (all-day when the time is unknown), the hotel is an all-day span from check-in to check-out, and selected local events cover their dates. Times are floating — they read as local time at the destination; a flight's description also gives its local arrival time and booking link. Event IDs come from the saved plan's id (or, for an unsaved plan, its route, dates and name), so two plans never overwrite each other's events and renaming a saved plan keeps its IDs. How a calendar app treats a re-import of the same file varies — some skip events they already have, some update them. Selected walking tours are not exported to the calendar, because tours carry no dates.
  • Print / PDF opens a clean, printable page of the whole plan (buildPlanPrintHtml in frontend/src/utils/planPrint.js): cost breakdown, flights, hotel, day-by-day itinerary, activities, places, free walking tours, events, SIM, transport and tips. Print it or choose Save as PDF in the print dialog. All plan text is HTML-escaped, only http(s) booking links are kept, and the page carries a Content-Security-Policy that lets nothing run except its own print button.

When a saved plan is loaded into a drawer, export (and the cost breakdown, budget status and saving) use that plan's trip details and itinerary snapshot — never the itinerary of the search currently on screen, which may be a different trip.

docs.title: Saved plans
docs.text:
Plans are stored in the plans table through /api/plans (list, create, get, rename/update, delete; each user sees only their own). The drawer can save, rename, load and delete plans, and the current plan can be dragged onto the saved-plans drop zone. Saving records Taste Graph signals (see Personalization).

A saved plan embeds a snapshot of the generated itinerary (days and estimated cost) alongside the selections, so reopening a plan months later shows the schedule as it was, including moves, edits and notes. Live verification evidence (link_verified, link_checked) is stripped from saved items, because it belongs to the live search. While a saved plan is loaded, itinerary editing is off until the user starts a new plan.

PlanViewModal shows a saved plan in full (flights per leg, hotel, the day-by-day itinerary and every selected item), each removable individually.

docs.title: Share links
docs.text:
Share calls POST /api/plans/{id}/share, which creates a random token (or returns the existing one), and copies ${origin}/share/<token> to the clipboard. Anyone with the link can open it without logging in.

GET /api/share/{token} returns a sanitised plan: the name, timestamps, the selections and only these search fields: origin, destination(s), dates, interests, traveller counts and pace. Nationality, visas, residence permits, accessibility needs and budget are dropped.

frontend/src/pages/SharePage.jsx renders a read-only trip card:

  • Route header (origin → stops in journey order) and dates
  • Flights (each leg with airline, times and price), hotel and cost summary
  • The arranged day-by-day itinerary, including edits and notes
  • Activities, free walking tours, events, SIM plan, transport picks and tips

Download as PNG draws the whole share page onto a canvas sized to fit (one pass measures and wraps every line, a second pass paints it) and downloads a single image, with no external libraries or server round-trip.

DELETE /api/plans/{id}/share revokes a link, but no UI calls it yet; it is available through the API only.

docs.title: Backend tests
docs.text:
cd backend
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt   # pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, ruff, bandit, pip-audit
python3 -m pytest -q
  • tests/conftest.py points DATA_DIR at a temporary directory (deleted at exit), sets a JWT secret, RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and an empty BACKUP_BUCKET, and seeds the place data once per session.
  • pyproject.toml sets asyncio_mode = "auto". Tests mock the Anthropic API; they make no real LLM calls.
  • tests/test_golden_places_runtime.py runs the 693-case golden set (tests/data/golden_places.csv) against place resolution and autocomplete and forbids web calls. tests/test_build_place_data.py checks the place-data generator. See Place and Airport Data.
  • Coverage, as CI runs it:

bash DATA_DIR=/tmp/test-data ADMIN_PASSWORD=test-admin-pw \ python3 -m pytest --cov=app --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=70

Coverage omits the agent classes, the orchestrator and chat agent, static_results.py, web_tools.py, schemas/travel.py, the seeders, backup.py and database.py.

As of 2026-10-30: 3,794 passed, 1 skipped.

docs.title: Frontend tests
docs.text:
cd frontend
npm test                    # vitest run --passWithNoTests
npm run test:coverage       # with v8 coverage, as CI runs it

Tests are *.test.js(x) files next to the code, run with vitest in jsdom (configured in vite.config.js). On Node 20.18 vitest needs NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-require-module:

NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-require-module npx vitest run

As of 2026-10-30: 38 test files, 532 tests passed.

docs.title: Lint and format
docs.text:
Check Command Backend lint ruff check backend/ Backend format ruff format --check backend/ Frontend lint cd frontend && npx eslint src/ --max-warnings 0

Ruff 0.15.13 is pinned and selects E, W, F, I and UP (ignoring E501 and UP007). The ESLint config (frontend/eslint.config.js) has one substantive rule: lucide icons whose names shadow globals (Map, Image, History, Text, Option, Infinity, Navigation) must be imported under an alias, because a shadowed Map once crashed every multi-city search. There is no lint npm script.

Pre-commit (.pre-commit-config.yaml, install with make install-hooks): ruff lint (--fix) and format on backend/, trailing whitespace, end-of-file, merge-conflict markers, YAML/JSON checks and mixed line endings.

Makefile targets (run from the repo root): install (backend requirements plus npm ci), install-hooks, format, lint (ruff and ESLint), security (bandit, pip-audit, npm audit), test (both suites with coverage), and ci (lint + security + test). Note that make security still ignores PYSEC-2025-185 and PYSEC-2025-183, which CI no longer ignores.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: All in .github/workflows/.

docs.title: ci.yml
docs.text:
Runs on every push to any branch and on pull requests to main.

Job What it does lint-backend ruff check and ruff format --check lint-frontend eslint with --max-warnings 0 security bandit -ll --skip B105,B106,B608; pip-audit (ignoring PYSEC-2023-62); npm audit --audit-level=high test-backend Python 3.12, pytest with coverage ≥ 70% test-frontend Node 20, npm run test:coverage build-and-scan Needs all of the above. Builds both images (docker build -f backend/Dockerfile . and docker build frontend/) and scans them with Trivy 0.70.0, failing on unfixed CRITICAL findings (.trivyignore lists accepted ones)

docs.title: docs.yml
docs.text:
Runs on push to main and by hand. Installs mkdocs, mkdocstrings[python], mkdocs-material and ghp-import, runs mkdocs build from mkdocs.yml, copies docs_homepage/index.html over site/index.html, and publishes site/ to the gh-pages branch, served at https://rupakc.github.io/travel-planner/. The custom homepage therefore replaces docs/index.md at the site root; the docs pages live under it (for example /Home/, /Architecture/).

To check the docs locally:

pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]"
mkdocs build --strict      # or: mkdocs serve

docs.title: deploy.yml
docs.text: Manual only and marked decommissioned. See Deployment.

docs.title: Trip Planning Features
docs.text: What a user can do in the app, and where each feature lives in the code. Chat, multi-city routing, personalization and plan sharing have their own pages: Chat Assistant, Multi-City Trips, Personalization and Sharing and Plans.

docs.title: App shell
docs.text:
• Routes (frontend/src/App.jsx): /login, /share/:token (public), /change-password, and the signed-in layout with / (Search and Results), /chat, /preferences and /admin (admins only). Any other path redirects to /.
  • Search, Results and Chat stay mounted and are hidden with CSS, so a running search or chat stream survives switching tabs. Logging out clears all search state.
  • A user who must change their password is sent to /change-password first.
  • The footer credits the place data: "Place data © GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) · Airport data: OurAirports".

docs.title: Search page
docs.text: frontend/src/pages/SearchPage.jsx has three modes.

docs.title: "I know where I'm going"
docs.text:
• Route. From and To use the airport/place typeahead (components/ui/AirportSearch.jsx → GET /api/airports/search). "Add a stop on the way (multi-city)" adds up to 3 intermediate stops, each with optional nights (1–30). The To city is the final destination.
  • Trip. Departure and return dates, budget in USD, nationality (NationalitySearch → GET /api/nationalities/search), residence permits and existing visas, interests.
  • Travellers (TravelerPanel): adults 18–64, seniors 65+, children 5–17, infants 0–4, plus accessibility needs (wheelchair, visual, hearing, cognitive).
  • Discovery style slider (serendipity 0–1): Famous classics, Balanced mix, Hidden gems.
  • Submitting records a recent search and writes the fields back to Preferences. Saved preferences pre-fill the form on load; the budget category maps to USD as low 1000, medium 3000, high 8000.
  • There is no pace control on the form. pace (relaxed / balanced / packed) is set by the "Slow it down" remix or through the API.

docs.title: "Surprise me 🎲"
docs.text: Origin, nationality, dates, optional budget, interests and travellers. POST /api/discover returns 5 destinations. Each card shows city and country, a weather emoji and description, a visa badge (⚠️ when not confirmed by the static table), flight time, a rough cost range and why it matches. "Plan this trip →" fills in the known-destination form.

docs.title: "Compare ⚖️"
docs.text: Seeded once from the known-destination form. Takes 2–3 destinations plus shared trip fields, and makes one POST /api/compare/destination call per destination in parallel, each column with its own loading and error state and a Retry that re-runs only that column. Responses from an earlier run are ignored. components/CompareTable.jsx shows cost estimate, flight, hotel, weather, visa and the Travel Ease grade, marking the best value in each row (stacked cards on phones). "Plan this trip" runs that exact request as a normal full search. Pure helpers are in utils/compare.js. Compare is single-city only (multi-city requests get 422).

docs.title: Recent searches
docs.text: A collapsible strip above the known-destination form (components/RecentSearches.jsx). Its open/closed state is remembered per browser. Clicking a card loads the whole search (route, stops, dates, travellers, budget, visas) into the form; "Search again" re-runs it; each card can be deleted. Past dates are moved to start a week from today with the same trip length. The backend keeps the newest 8 per user and merges identical searches, ignoring interest order (/api/recent-searches).

docs.title: Onboarding tour
docs.text: A first-run tooltip tour (components/OnboardingTour.jsx, hooks/useFirstRunTour.js, utils/tour.js). It opens once, 400 ms after load, for users with no recent searches, and only on the Search page in known-destination mode. Six steps: recent searches, route, interests, Preferences, the plan button and My Plan. A step whose element is not on screen is skipped. Each step is a focus-trapped dialog (Esc closes it). Completion is stored in localStorage['tp_tour_done:<username>']; "New here? Take a quick tour" replays it.

docs.title: Results page
docs.text: frontend/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx. Results stream through services/api.js → workers/sseWorker.js. The header shows progress (completed/16) and a status chip per agent (searching, enhancing, done, error) that links to its section. If the stream ends without done, the page reports that the connection was interrupted.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
In display order (AGENT_ORDER):

Section What it shows Flights Outbound and return legs, airline, stops, price and booking link; one group per leg on multi-city trips. Pricing-advisor banner with sparkline, Google Flights price-insights chip, opt-in fare calendar. Filters: max stops, max price, departure and arrival windows (/api/flights/filtered). A Layover button per connection opens a layover mini-plan (POST /api/layover). Weather Forecast Day cards; Open-Meteo data within 16 days, else an LLM estimate; grouped per stay on multi-city trips. Hotels Options across budget tiers. Filters: beds, max price per night, wifi, distance from centre, private washroom (/api/hotels/filtered). Activities Interest-matched activities with price and rating, and weather hints. Filters: interests, max price, availability dates, min rating (/api/activities/filtered). Places to See Landmarks and sights; Google Places data when SERPER_KEY is set. Free Walking Tours Crawled tours (GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, FreeWalkingTour.com, SANDEMANs NewEurope), top picks first per city, each linking to the provider's tour page (components/WalkingToursSection.jsx). What's On Festivals, concerts and markets during the trip; ~ marks a typical-season date. Visa Entry requirement, permitted stay, fee, documents and official link. SIM Cards Local SIMs and global eSIMs. Travel Tips Safety, culture, scams, money. Emergency Card Per-city police, ambulance and fire numbers, embassy, phrases and local laws; printable. Getting Around Local and inter-city transport options. Currency & Forex Exchange rates, where to exchange, card, cash and ATM advice. Itinerary Day-by-day plan with Cards and Timeline views (components/TimelineView.jsx) and a route map (components/TripMap.jsx, Leaflet with OpenStreetMap tiles). See Itinerary. Trip Health Check The stress test: a score ring, issues with suggested fixes, and a re-check of the edited plan. Packing List Weather- and activity-aware checklist; checkbox state is kept in the browser, and items can be added to the plan.

Above the sections:

  • Travel Ease banner (ConfidenceBanner): the Phase 0 grade from the static destination scores.
  • Search panel to edit and re-run the search.
  • Trip Remix (RemixBar, utils/remix.js): five presets — A week later, Half the budget, Make it luxe, Slow it down (relaxed pace), Long weekend. Each re-plans the trip and shows a before/after banner.

On multi-city trips every list is stable-sorted into journey order (utils/orderSectionByCity.js).

docs.title: Verification badges
docs.text: Each section header shows a chip from data.verification (components/VerificationBadge.jsx): Verified, Partly verified, AI-generated, Check details, or a spinning Checking… while hotel, activity and place links are still being checked. Clicking the chip opens a popover with the summary and each check (pass, fail or note, with its source link). Visa and emergency conflicts also show a banner in the section body, and items whose link was matched by name get a "Found online" tag. When the stream ends with a chip still pending, utils/verification.js resolves it. Saved plans drop the live link evidence. Chat does not show badges. The rules are in Agent System.

docs.title: Best-value package
docs.text: Shown once the search has finished (utils/bestValuePackage.js, components/BestValuePackage.jsx). Deterministic rules, no extra agent: a balanced flight per leg, one well-reviewed 3–4 star hotel, cheap or free activities (2 per city, 4 in total), free walking tours (up to 3) and places (2 per city, 4 in total), and a SIM plan covering the trip. Every pick is a real listed item. "Add all to My Plan" merges them in one update without duplicates, and Undo restores the previous selections. Its total uses the drawer's cost arithmetic. It is disabled while a saved plan is open.

docs.title: Budget planner
docs.text: Shown after the best-value package when the search has a budget (utils/budgetPlanner.js, components/BudgetPlanner.jsx). It runs entirely in the browser. The budget is split per person into Flights, Stay and Activities sliders ($10 steps) plus a read-only "Everything else". Defaults: the cheapest fare (summed per leg on multi-city), median nightly rate × nights, and 15% for activities; if those overshoot, activities shrink first, then stay. Under each slider it counts what fits ("6 of 12 hotels fit"). Once the user touches it, over-budget hotel and flight cards are dimmed and tagged, and "Show only what fits" can hide them (selected cards always stay visible). When fewer than 3 hotels fit, Find cheaper hotels runs the hotel filter with the stay share per night; this is the only action that calls the API. Reset restores the defaults; a new search or remix resets everything.

docs.title: Fare calendar and price insights
docs.text:
• Fare calendar (components/FareCalendarStrip.jsx, utils/fareCalendar.js). A "Fare calendar" button in the Flights header, offered only when GET /health reports serpapi_configured, the user is signed in and the trip is single-city. It loads POST /api/flights/fare-calendar: seven cells for departure dates ±3 days with the trip length kept the same, each with the cheapest live fare and its difference from the chosen dates; the cheapest is highlighted. Clicking another date asks for confirmation, then runs a new search with both dates shifted.
  • Price insights. When live fares come with Google's verdict, a chip reads, for example, "Fares are low right now · typical $420–$610" (green, grey or amber for low, typical or high). This is Google's data, not an AI estimate.
  • Pricing advisor. The deferred agent's banner: whether prices look high or low for the route, when to book, and a sparkline.

docs.title: Itinerary
docs.text:
components/ItinerarySection.jsx, with helpers in utils/.

  • Drag-and-drop. Activities can be dragged (grip handle) to another day or time of day. The drag uses a custom MIME type so the plan drawer never mistakes it for a plan drop. Each activity also has a Move menu for keyboard and touch users, listing every valid target. Moving onto an occupied slot swaps the two; on multi-city trips moves stay within the same city. Removed activities appear under "Removed" with Restore. The toolbar has Undo (last 20 actions) and Reset, and empty slots show "Free time".
  • Layout overlay. Moves are not written into the itinerary. utils/itineraryLayout.js stores an overlay keyed by each activity's original slot ("<day>-<time_of_day>") and fingerprinted to the itinerary, saved as selections.itinerary_layout. Timeline view, the map, exports, shared plans and the saved-plan viewer all show the arranged itinerary. An overlay whose fingerprint does not match is ignored.
  • Timed schedule. utils/schedule.js estimates start and end times for each activity from its slot (anchors 09:00, 13:30, 18:30), its duration_hours and the travel time from the previous stop (walking up to 1.5 km, else transit, from the slots' coordinates; a 20-minute buffer without them). Times are always derived, never stored, and the UI says they are estimates. A day that starts activities more than 45 minutes late or runs past 23:00 gets a "Tight schedule" note. Activities picked into My Plan keep their scheduled times ("Day 2 · Afternoon · 13:30–16:00").
  • Edits and notes. A slot's activity, location and cost can be edited (selections.itinerary_edits), and notes added (selections.itinerary_notes). Editing is off, with the reason shown, while a saved plan is loaded.
  • Health check. The stress-test agent audits the generated itinerary. After the user rearranges or edits it, Re-check my edited plan sends the arranged itinerary with edits and times, plus current flights, visa and weather (utils/stressTestPayload.js), to POST /api/stress-test. The result replaces the findings on screen; a later change shows "Your plan changed since this check", and errors keep the previous findings.

docs.title: My Plan drawer
docs.text: On both Results (MyPlanDrawer) and Chat (ChatPlanDrawer). Users pick flights (one per leg on multi-city trips), a hotel, activities, places, walking tours, events, a SIM plan, tips, transport options, packing-list items and itinerary slots. The drawer shows a cost breakdown, exports to calendar and print/PDF, and saves, loads and shares plans. Details: Sharing and Plans.

docs.title: Chat, Preferences, Admin and feedback
docs.text:
• Chat: see Chat Assistant.
  • Preferences (pages/PreferencesPage.jsx): Travel Budget, Identity (nationality, current residence, used as the default departure city), Documents (permits, visas), Travel Style (interests, travellers, accessibility), and a Taste Graph card with Reset. Bound two ways to the Search form; see Personalization.
  • Admin (pages/AdminPage.jsx, admins only): a Users tab to create users with a temporary password (at least 8 characters; they must change it on first login), list them, deactivate, reactivate and reset passwords; and a Feedback tab, filterable by page, category and minimum rating.
  • Feedback widget (components/FeedbackWidget.jsx): on every signed-in page. 1–5 stars, a category (bug, feature request, general, praise) and an optional message up to 500 characters, sent to POST /api/feedback.
  • Rate limits: when a limit is hit, the API's 429 message ("Too many requests — please wait N seconds and try again.") is shown as-is (utils/httpError.js). Defaults per 10 minutes: 10 searches, 30 chat messages, 30 compare calls, 10 discover calls, 60 single-agent calls.

docs.title: Free Walking Tours Section Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: A new "Free Walking Tours" section on the Results page, right after "Places to See". It recommends free walking tours for each destination city, found by crawling GuruWalk, FreeTour.com, SANDEMANs NewEurope and FreeWalkingTour.com. Every card links to the original tour page.

Architecture: - A deterministic crawler service fetches each provider's public city page, then parses structured data (JSON-LD Event) or HTML cards into one normalized tour shape. - A new specialist agent, WalkingToursAgent, runs the crawl per destination city. It asks the LLM (Haiku, via BaseAgent.execute) to pick and explain the best tours for this traveler, choosing by candidate id only. URLs always come from the crawl and never from the LLM. - If the LLM fails, a rating-based ranking is used, so a successful crawl never yields a blank section. - The agent streams as a normal Phase-1 section (type: "walking_tours"). - The frontend adds a section component plus full My Plan support: drawer, saved-plan viewer, share page and print.

Tech Stack: FastAPI, httpx (async), BeautifulSoup4, ddgs (fallback discovery), pytest; React 18, Tailwind, vitest (+ jsdom).

Spec: the user request and the design in this conversation, summarised in "Design facts" below.

docs.title: Design facts (verified against the live sites, 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Provider key Display name City page Parse Notes guruwalk GuruWalk https://www.guruwalk.com/{slug} JSON-LD @type: Event (≈10/page): name, url, image, description, aggregateRating{ratingValue, reviewCount}, offers{price:0} robots disallows /search; city pages allowed freetour FreeTour.com https://www.freetour.com/{slug} JSON-LD Event, same fields robots allows user-initiated agents; only /company/, /booking/, /account/ disallowed freewalkingtour FreeWalkingTour.com https://freewalkingtour.com/{slug}/ HTML cards a.relative.block.h-full (href /{slug}/{tour}/); card text e.g. "Pay what you wish Welcome to Barcelona: Old Town and Modernism 4.9 116 reviews 2h 30m Book now"; image src may be relative /_ipx/... Keep only cards containing "Pay what you wish" (others are paid private tours). Unknown city → HTTP 500 sandemans SANDEMANs NewEurope https://www.neweuropetours.eu/sandemans-tours/{slug}/ a[href*="/sandemans-tours/{slug}/"] with link text; keep titles containing "free" (case-insensitive), dedupe by href Paid "Private Tour" links must be dropped
  • Unknown cities return 404 (or 500 on freewalkingtour). Treat any non-200 response as status "none" for that provider.
  • Requests use the honest User-Agent VoyagerTravelPlanner/1.0 (trip-planning assistant; fetches city tour listings on behalf of a user). It is accepted by all four sites.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• The section key is walking_tours everywhere: SSE type, AGENT_ORDER, selections key, agent name and .agents/walking_tours.md.
  • It is placed immediately after places_to_see in AGENT_ORDER and in the orchestrator lists.
  • LLM output never supplies URLs. The prompt says so, and the code ignores any URL the LLM returns. Card links are crawled URLs whose host matches the provider's domain.
  • Agent prompts always pair each city with its country (repo rule; see docs/agents.md "How to add a new agent").
  • Fetch only the four city-page URL patterns above. One request per provider per city, timeout 12 s, all providers in parallel, results cached in get_cache() under walking_tours:{provider}:{slug}.
  • Chat is knowledge-only: no chat wiring.
  • No new dependencies (httpx, bs4 and ddgs are already in backend/requirements.txt).
  • Frontend links use target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" and pass through safeUrl (exported from frontend/src/utils/planPrint.js).
  • Copy: section label Free Walking Tours; badge label Walking Tours; price notes are Free · tip-based (guruwalk, freetour, sandemans) and Pay what you wish (freewalkingtour).

docs.title: Data contract (backend produces, frontend consumes)
docs.text:
{
  "results": [{
    "id": "guruwalk-barcelona-0",
    "name": "Free Tour of the Old Town",
    "provider": "GuruWalk",
    "provider_key": "guruwalk",
    "url": "https://www.guruwalk.com/walks/564-free-tour-...",
    "image_url": "https://media.guruwalk.com/...",
    "description": "…",
    "rating": 4.9, "review_count": 1234,
    "duration": "2h 30m",
    "price_note": "Free · tip-based",
    "city": "Barcelona",
    "reason": "Covers the Gothic Quarter — matches your history interest",
    "top_pick": true
  }],

}
  • status is one of "ok" | "none" | "error".
  • If every provider for every city returns "error", the agent returns {"error": "..."}.
  • rating, review_count, duration, image_url, description and reason may be null.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
1. Destination formats. "Tokyo, Japan (HND)", "Kraków" (diacritics), "New York City" and a bare IATA code all need a usable slug, plus discovery when the slug misses. → test_city_slug_* and test_split_city_country_* in Task 1, and test_discovery_fallback_used_on_404 in Task 2.
  2. Malformed provider pages. Broken JSON-LD, missing fields, non-numeric ratings, relative image URLs or HTML changes must yield fewer cards, never a crash or an error for the whole section. → test_parse_*_tolerates_* in Task 1.
  3. LLM misbehaviour. Unknown ids, duplicate ids, invented URLs, an {"error"} result or empty recommendations. Cards must still show (heuristic fallback), with only crawled URLs. → test_agent_* in Task 3.
  4. Partial outages. One or more providers time out or are blocked: the section shows what was found. Only a total failure is an error. → test_fetch_city_tours_partial_failure and test_all_providers_fail_returns_error in Tasks 2–3.
  5. Untrusted links in the UI. A javascript: or other-domain URL in data must not render as a live link. → walking tours card never renders unsafe links in Task 5.

docs.title: Task 1: Provider parsers and city helpers (pure functions)
docs.text:
Files: - Create: backend/app/services/walking_tours.py - Test: backend/tests/test_walking_tours_parsers.py, with small handwritten HTML fixtures inline in the test (mirroring the structures in Design facts; never committed copies of the real pages)

Interfaces — Produces: - PROVIDERS: dict[str, dict] keyed by provider key, each holding name, domain, city_url: Callable[[str], str], price_note - city_slug(city: str) -> str: NFKD → ASCII; lowercase; anything outside [a-z0-9] becomes a single -; strip leading and trailing - - split_city_country(destination: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]: drops a trailing (XXX) IATA code, splits on the first comma, strips whitespace - parse_jsonld_tours(html: str, provider_key: str, city: str) -> list[dict] - parse_freewalkingtour(html: str, slug: str, city: str) -> list[dict] - parse_sandemans(html: str, slug: str, city: str) -> list[dict] - All parsers return tour dicts in the data-contract shape, with id = f"{provider_key}-{slug}-{n}", reason=None, top_pick=False. They keep only URLs whose host equals or ends with the provider domain, cap at 10 tours, drop duplicate URLs, and never raise (they return [] on garbage).

docs.title: Task 2: Crawler: fetch, discovery fallback, caching
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: backend/app/services/walking_tours.py - Test: backend/tests/test_walking_tours_fetch.py

Interfaces: - Consumes: Task 1. - Produces: async def fetch_city_tours(city: str, *, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]], which returns (tours, sources). sources has one entry per provider, in the shape of the data contract. - Providers are fetched in parallel (asyncio.gather), with a 12 s timeout each and the User-Agent from Design facts. - A non-200 response gives "none"; an exception or timeout gives "error". - Results are cached per (provider, slug) with get_cache(); failures are not cached. - Discovery fallback: when a guruwalk or freetour city page returns non-200, run one ddgs text search site:{domain} {city} free walking tour, executed off the event loop. Take the first result URL that matches ^https://www\.{domain}/[a-z0-9-]+/?$, fetch it and parse it. If nothing is found, the status stays "none".

docs.title: Task 3: WalkingToursAgent, agent definition, orchestrator, route, schema
docs.text:
Files: - Create: .agents/walking_tours.md, with frontmatter name: walking_tours, a description, tools: [] and max_turns: 1. The body follows the events.md / places.md conventions: a "What to Find" section, a "Rules" section, and an output example of the recommendation JSON below. It must state "Never output URLs". - Create: backend/app/agents/walking_tours_agent.py, class WalkingToursAgent(BaseAgent) with __init__(self, agents_dir) and async def run(self, request: TravelSearchRequest) -> dict - Create: backend/app/api/routes/walking_tours.py, POST /walking-tours, mirroring routes/events.py - Modify: backend/app/main.py: register the router with tag walking_tours - Modify: backend/app/agents/orchestrator.py: - import and self.walking_tours = WalkingToursAgent(agents_dir) - in run(), add it to the gather after self.events.run(request), as walking_tours = safe(phase1_results[10], {"results": []}), and add "walking_tours" to the returned dict after "places_to_see" - in stream_run(), add it to the agent_status list after "places_to_see" and add "walking_tours": self.walking_tours to phase1_agents - Modify: backend/app/schemas/travel.py: add WalkingTour, WalkingTourSource and WalkingToursResponse per the data contract, and walking_tours: dict = {} on TravelSearchResponse - Test: backend/tests/test_walking_tours_agent.py

Interfaces: - Consumes: fetch_city_tours, split_city_country from Tasks 1–2. - Recommendation format the LLM returns: {"recommendations": [{"id": str, "reason": str, "top_pick": bool}]}, best first. - run() behaviour: 1. Determine the cities: request.destinations if multi-city, else [request.destination]. 2. Crawl every city concurrently. 3. If every source has status error, return {"error": "Couldn't reach the walking-tour sites right now"}. 4. If no tours were found, return {"results": [], "sources": [...]} without calling the LLM. 5. Otherwise build the prompt: - each city with its country (use split_city_country, and add "(identify the country)" when it is None) - interests, request.traveler_context and request.serendipity_context - when multi-city, the coverage rule "4–6 per city" - one line per candidate: id | name | provider | rating | reviews | duration | description[:200] - ask for 4–8 picks per city, at most 2 top_pick per city, and a reason of at most 20 words tied to the traveler 6. Merge the answer: keep only known ids, the first occurrence of each, in the LLM's order, setting reason and top_pick from it. Any URL-like field from the LLM is ignored. 7. If the LLM returned an error, or nothing usable remains: rank by rating * log1p(review_count) (unknown values last), keep 8 per city, reason=None, top_pick=False. 8. Return {"results": [...], "sources": [...]}.

docs.title: Best-Value Package Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: A "Best-value package" card on the Results page that picks a sensible, cheap set of real results (flight, hotel, activities, free walking tour, free places, SIM) and adds them all to My Plan in one click, with Undo.

Architecture: Pure, rule-based derivation in the browser from the results already streamed (results[agent]): no new agent, no backend change. A pure module builds the package and merges it into selections; a presentational component renders it; ResultsPage computes it with useMemo once the search is done and applies it with one setSelections call.

Tech Stack: React 18, Tailwind 4, lucide-react icons, vitest + jsdom (no testing-library; createRoot + act).

Spec: Backlog item #26 in Future_Improvements.md ("Virtual Interlining and Package Deals" → "Best Value Package" card). Design decisions below were made by Claude (user delegated all choices); facts about data shapes come from /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-26.md.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) a new LLM agent that composes a package — rejected: extra latency and cost, and it could recommend items that are not in the results; (b) deterministic rules over the streamed results — chosen: instant, testable, and every pick is a real listed item with a link.

Pick rules (all numbers coerced with Number() + Number.isFinite; anything non-finite is "unknown"; any results[x] that has an error key or no list is treated as empty):

  • Flight (single-city: results.flights.results; multi-city: each results.flights.legs[i].results, one pick per leg). Candidates: price_usd > 0. If any candidate has source !== 'estimate', drop the 'estimate' ones. Let P = cheapest price. Pool = candidates with price ≤ P × 1.15. Sort pool by total stops asc ((outbound?.stops ?? stops ?? 0) + (return?.stops ?? 0)), then total duration asc (outbound?.duration_minutes ?? duration_minutes + return?.duration_minutes, unknown last), then price asc. Reason: "Cheapest fare" if its price equals P, else "Fewer stops or shorter for $D more than the cheapest fare" (D rounded).
  • Hotel (one only — selections.hotel holds a single hotel). Candidates: price_per_night_usd > 0. Multi-city (searchData.destinations?.length > 1): restrict to hotels whose city equals searchData.destinations[0] when any match. Stars = Math.round(star_rating). Pool = stars 3; if empty stars 4; if empty all candidates. Sort by review_score desc (unknown last), then nightly price asc. Reason: "Mid-range (3★), best-reviewed in its class" (use the actual star count; add the city name for multi-city).
  • Budget fit. If searchData.budget_usd > 0 and the package total is over budget, swap the hotel for the cheapest candidate (same city restriction) whose review_score is unknown or ≥ 7, if that is cheaper; reason becomes "Cheaper stay to fit your budget". Do nothing else to fit the budget.
  • Activities. Candidates: price known and 0 ≤ price ≤ 30. Sort by similarity_score desc (unknown last), then price asc. Up to 3 per city (a.city ?? ''), 6 overall. Reason: "Free" or "$12", plus " · matches your interests" when similarity_score >= 0.5.
  • Free walking tour. One per city (top_pick first, then highest rating), 3 overall. Reason: the tour's price_note.
  • Free places to see. admission_fee_usd coerces to exactly 0; top 2 by rating per city, 4 overall. Reason: "Free entry".
  • SIM. Candidates from results.sim.plans with price_usd > 0. Trip days = whole days between departure and return + 1 (null when either date is missing). Prefer plans with validity_days unknown or ≥ trip days; cheapest of those, else cheapest overall. Reason: "Covers your N-day trip" or "Cheapest plan".
  • Not included: events, getting-around, tips, itinerary slots.
  • No package (return null) unless it has a flight or a hotel.
  • Total = computePlanCost(pkg.selections, searchData) and budget = getBudgetStatus(total, searchData.budget_usd), so the card matches the My Plan drawer exactly. The card states "Flight prices are per person" (same convention as the flights section).

Applying: - One setSelections merge (never repeated handleSelect: its toggles would remove already-picked items). flight, hotel, sim are replaced; multi-city flights replace only the legs the package covers; activities, places_to_see, walking_tours are unioned without duplicates (identity: name, name, url). Nothing else is touched. - If the package will replace a different flight, hotel or SIM the user already picked, the card says so before they click ("Replaces your current hotel and SIM."). - After applying: button shows "Added to My Plan" (disabled) plus Undo, which restores the exact selections from just before the click. The undo snapshot is cleared by a new search/remix. - While a saved plan from the drawer is open (loadedPlanSearchData is non-null), applying is disabled with a short reason, because the open plan may be a different trip. - Placement: Results page, directly after "Remix this trip", only when isDone; it recomputes when results change (filters re-stream sections). - Analytics: track('best_value_package_applied', 'results', { items }) and track('best_value_package_undone', 'results', {}).

Non-goals: ChatPage (chat is knowledge-only), saved-plan viewer, share page, backend changes, per-traveller multiplication of prices (the drawer doesn't do it either).

docs.title: Drag-and-Drop Itinerary Editing Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: On the Results page itinerary, let users move an activity to another day or time of day (drag-and-drop, plus a keyboard/touch "Move to…" menu), swap two activities, remove one, undo, and reset — with every edit, note, plan pick, export, print view, share page and saved plan following the activity to its new place.

Architecture: A pure layout overlay selections.itinerary_layout records only where each moved/removed activity now sits, keyed by the activity's original slot key ("<day_number>-<time_of_day>", the de-facto ID the whole app already uses). One pure function, arrangeItinerary(itinerary, layout), turns the original itinerary plus the overlay into the arranged days; every reader renders those arranged days and looks up edits/notes by slot.key (the original key), so nothing is re-keyed on a move. The overlay carries a fingerprint of the itinerary it was made for and is ignored when it doesn't match (stream retry, a saved plan for another trip).

Tech Stack: React 18, native HTML5 drag-and-drop (no new library — the codebase already uses native DnD), Tailwind 4, vitest + jsdom (createRoot + act).

Spec: Backlog item #12 in Future_Improvements.md ("Drag-and-Drop Itinerary Editing"). Facts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-12.md. All design choices below are Claude's (the user delegated them).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: - (a) Overlay of positions keyed by original slot key — chosen. Edits/notes/plan picks/.ics UIDs (slot-${key}) stay attached to the activity with zero re-keying; old saved plans need nothing; one function to test. - (b) Rewrite selections.itinerary and re-key edits/notes/itinerary_slots on every move — rejected: every move mutates four structures, .ics UIDs change (calendar duplicates), and the live Results itinerary is not selections.itinerary. - (c) A DnD library (dnd-kit) — rejected: new dependency; native DnD is the codebase convention and the "Move to…" menu covers touch/keyboard.

Model: - slotKey(dayNumber, timeOfDay) = \${dayNumber}-${timeOfDay}`. Positions are the three standard timesmorning,afternoon,eveningon each existing day. A slot whosetime_of_dayis not one of the three is displayed where it is and is not movable. -itinerary_layout = { fingerprint: string, positions: { [originalKey]: "-" | null } }—null= removed; a key absent frompositionsstays at its original position.EMPTY_SELECTIONS.itinerary_layout = null. Old plans without it behave exactly as today. -fingerprint= short stable hash of the original itinerary'sday_number|time_of_day|activitylines. A layout whose fingerprint differs from the itinerary being rendered is ignored (rendered as the original) and not written to. - **Move** = put activity A at target position T. If T holds activity B, B moves to A's current position (swap). If T is empty (removed/free), A just moves. Moving to its own position is a no-op. Every day keeps at most one activity per time of day (TimelineView, .ics and print rely on this). - **City rule (multi-city):** a move is allowed only when the source day'scityand the target day'scityare equal (case-insensitive, first comma segment) or either is missing. Swaps must satisfy the rule both ways. - **Remove** = positionnull; the spot shows "Free time" and accepts drops. **Restore** puts a removed activity back at its original position if that is empty, else in the first empty position of its original day, else it stays removed (button disabled with a tooltip). - **Arranged days:** same days, same order and day metadata (date, theme, city); each day's slots = activities now positioned there, sorted morning → afternoon → evening, each slot object is the original slot pluskey(original key) andtime_of_day(its new time).removed: [{ key, slot }]lists removed activities for the UI. - **Costs:** for a day whose contents changed,daily_estimated_cost_usd= sum of its slots' cost (itinerary_edits[key].cost ?? slot.estimated_cost_usd, finite numbers only); untouched days keep the original value.total_estimated_cost_usdis recomputed the same way only when anything changed. Unchanged itinerary → identical numbers to today. - **Plan picks follow:** after every move/remove/restore/undo/reset, eachitinerary_slotsentry is updated to its activity's currentday_number/time_of_day(entries for removed activities are kept, unchanged — the user removes them from the drawer as today). - **Undo:** an in-memory stack of previous layouts (max 20) in ResultsPage; "Undo" reverts the last move/remove/restore. **Reset** clears the layout (with Undo able to bring it back). Both cleared by a new search/remix. - **Where editing happens:** Cards view itinerary only (it is already the edit/notes view). Timeline view, TripMap, drawer, PlanViewModal, SharePage, .ics and print all *display* the arranged itinerary. ChatPage is untouched (chat is knowledge-only; its itinerary is a different shape). - **Health Check:** when the layout has changes, the Trip Health Check section shows one line: "Checked against the original itinerary — your moves aren't re-checked." - **Interaction:** - Each movable slot row has a drag handle (GripVertical,cursor-grab) and isdraggable; drag data uses the custom MIMEapplication/x-itinerary-slot(neverapplication/json, which the drawer treats as a plan). Valid drop targets (other slots and Free-time spots, honouring the city rule) highlight on dragover; invalid ones don't accept the drop. - Each movable slot has a "Move" button opening a small menu listing every valid target as "Day N · Morning" (swaps labelled "Day N · Morning (swap with <activity>)") plus "Remove from day". Fully keyboard operable; Escape closes it; focus returns to the button. - Section toolbar (only when the layout has changes): "N changes" · Undo · Reset. Removed activities listed under "Removed" with Restore. - Status messages in anaria-live="polite"region, e.g. "Moved Sagrada Família to Day 2 · Afternoon". - **Analytics:**track('itinerary_slot_moved', 'results', { method: 'drag'|'menu', swap: bool }),track('itinerary_slot_removed', 'results', {}),track('itinerary_layout_reset', 'results', {})`.

Non-goals: ChatPage itinerary, re-running the Health Check, adding new activities, more than one activity per time of day, editing in Timeline view, backend changes.

docs.title: Trip Comparison Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Let a user compare 2–3 destinations side by side for the same origin, dates and travellers — estimated trip cost, cheapest flight, typical hotel price, weather, visa, safety and ease — then start the full plan for the one they pick with one click.

Architecture: A new lightweight backend endpoint POST /api/compare/destination summarises ONE destination by running only the decision-relevant agents (flights, hotels, weather; visa only when the static table can't answer) in parallel plus the instant static scores, then reducing them to a compact summary with a pure, unit-tested function. The frontend adds a third Search-page mode, "Compare", that fires one request per destination in parallel and fills each column as it arrives.

Tech Stack: FastAPI + Pydantic v2, existing agents (FlightsAgent, HotelsAgent, WeatherAgent, VisaAgent), static tables in backend/app/agents/static_results.py, in-memory TTL cache (backend/app/core/cache.py); React 18 + Tailwind; pytest (asyncio_mode=auto), vitest.

Spec: Backlog item #1 in Future_Improvements.md ("Trip Comparison / Side-by-Side View"). Facts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-1-28.md Part A. Design choices are Claude's (user delegated them).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: - (a) Run two or three full /api/search streams side by side — rejected: ~17 LLM calls each through a process-wide semaphore of 6 (each search ~2× slower), minutes of waiting, and the Results page holds only one result set. - (b) Reuse Discover (one LLM call guessing costs) — rejected: estimates only, no real flights/weather; exactly the "is this real?" problem. - (c) Per-destination lightweight summary endpoint — chosen: ~2–3 LLM calls per destination (flights unless SerpAPI is configured, hotels, visa only if not in the static table, weather only for cities Open-Meteo can't serve), real weather, static scores instant; parallel per destination; cacheable per request.

Backend: - POST /api/compare/destination, auth required like other routes, body = TravelSearchRequest (single destination; destinations must be null/≤1 — multi-city is rejected with 422 "Compare works with single destinations"). - Runs concurrently with per-piece timeouts: FlightsAgent.run (45 s), HotelsAgent.run (45 s; no enrich — URLs aren't needed for comparing), WeatherAgent.run (30 s), visa = get_static_visa(request) if it returns data else VisaAgent.run (30 s). A piece that fails or times out becomes null in the summary with its name listed in missing; the endpoint still returns 200 if at least one piece succeeded, else 502. - Summary (pure function summarize_destination(request, flights, hotels, weather, visa, confidence) -> dict in backend/app/services/compare.py): - destination (as given), label (city name: hotels/flights destination string's first comma segment if present, else request.destination) - flight: cheapest valid fare {price_usd, stops, duration_minutes, airline, source} where stops/duration sum outbound + return; price_usd > 0 finite only; prefer non-estimate sources when any exist. null if none. - hotel: {typical_nightly_usd, cheapest_good_nightly_usd, count} — typical = median nightly price of 3★–4★ hotels (fallback all priced hotels); cheapest_good = lowest nightly with review_score >= 7 (null if none). null if no priced hotels. - weather: {avg_high_c, avg_low_c, poor_days, total_days, source} from weather.days; null if no days. - visa: {visa_type, max_stay_days, fee_usd, processing_time, verified} — verified = True only when it came from the static table. - ease: from get_confidence_score(request): {total, grade, safety, english, infrastructure, visa_ease} (sub-score score values); null when the destination isn't in the table. - daily_cost_usd: the table's avg_daily_cost_usd for the destination (expose via a small helper next to get_confidence_score; null when unknown). - estimate: {total_usd, flight_usd, stay_usd, daily_usd, nights} per traveller — flight price + typical nightly × nights + daily cost × days (days = nights, min 1; nights from dates, default 7). Any missing part → that part null and total_usd = sum of known parts with partial: true. budget_status: 'under' | 'over' | null vs request.budget_usd. - missing: list of piece names that failed. - All numbers coerced defensively (strings/junk → ignored). - Cache: key "compare:" + md5(request.model_dump_json()) in the shared TTL cache; store only complete-enough results (≥1 piece) and never cache a 502. - Chat is untouched.

Frontend: - SearchPage mode toggle gains "Compare" (third button). Its form: origin, 2–3 destination fields (AirportSearch; "Add another" up to 3; remove ×), departure/return dates, nationality, budget, travellers, interests — prefilled from the known-mode form/preferences the same way Discover prefills. - On "Compare", one compareDestination(request) call per destination in parallel (new function in frontend/src/services/api.js, axios like the others); each column shows its own loading/error state ("Couldn't load — Retry"). - Comparison table (frontend/src/components/CompareTable.jsx): one column per destination; rows: Estimated trip cost per traveller (with budget chip; "partial" note), Cheapest flight (price · stops · duration · "estimate" badge when source is estimate), Hotel per night (typical / from), Weather (avg high/low °C, "N of M days poor", "climate estimate" when not Open-Meteo), Visa (type, fee, max stay; "Verified" vs "AI — check official site"), Travel Ease (total/100 + grade colour), Safety /20, English /20, Typical daily spend. Per numeric row the best value gets an emerald "Best" marker (lowest cost/price, fewest poor days, highest ease/safety/english); ties mark all; rows with <2 known values mark none. Mobile: columns become stacked cards (no horizontal page scroll at 375px). - Each column has "Plan this trip": switches to known mode with the form prefilled with that destination and the shared fields, and submits it (the normal full search). - Pure helpers in frontend/src/utils/compare.js: buildCompareRequests(form) -> TravelSearchRequest[], bestByRow(summaries) -> { [rowKey]: Set<index> }, formatters. Unit-tested. - Analytics: track('compare_run', 'search', { count }), track('compare_plan_clicked', 'search', { position }).

Non-goals: comparing saved plans, multi-city comparison, chat, sharing a comparison, more than 3 destinations.
