docs.title: Source Verification Labels Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Every Results section tells the traveller how much to trust it — "Verified" (real source or reference data agrees), "Partly verified" (some items confirmed online), "AI-generated — verify before booking", or "Conflicts with reference" — with the concrete checks behind the label, and hotel/activity/place cards show which items were found online.

Architecture: A pure backend function verify_section(name, data, request) derives a verification object from evidence the pipeline already produces — real data sources (Google Flights, Open-Meteo, crawled walking tours), the web searches enrichment already runs (now recorded per item as link_verified), and the curated static tables (visa, emergency numbers). The orchestrator attaches it to each section's data at every yield (initial, enriched, static), so it streams with the section, is cached with it, and needs no new event type. The frontend renders a chip in each section header with a popover of checks, plus per-item "Found online" badges.

Tech Stack: FastAPI orchestrator (SSE), existing enrichment (backend/app/agents/hotels_agent.py, backend/app/services/activity_url_resolver.py, backend/app/services/places_url_resolver.py), static tables (backend/app/agents/static_results.py); React 18 + Tailwind; pytest, vitest.

Spec: Backlog item #28 in Future_Improvements.md ("Hallucination Guardrails with Source Verification"). Facts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-1-28.md Part B. Design choices are Claude's (user delegated them).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: - (a) A second LLM pass that "checks" the first — rejected: an LLM verifying an LLM can hallucinate the verification, adds ~15 calls and latency per search. - (b) New per-item web searches/fetches for every claim — rejected for v1: competes with enrichment for the DuckDuckGo rate limit, fetching LLM-supplied URLs is an SSRF risk, and adds seconds. - (c) Evidence-based labels from data the pipeline already has — chosen: zero added latency or network calls, deterministic and testable, and honest: when there's no evidence the label says so.

verification object (attached as data["verification"] on every yielded section dict that has no error):

{ "level": "verified" | "partial" | "unverified" | "conflict",
  "label": short UI text,
  "summary": one sentence,
  "checks": [ { "label": str, "status": "pass" | "fail" | "info", "detail": str, "url": str | None } ],
  "items_verified": int | None, "items_total": int | None,
  "pending": bool }   # true on the first hotels/activities/places yield while enrichment still runs

Labels: verified → "Verified", partial → "Partly verified", unverified → "AI-generated", conflict → "Check details".

Per section (anything not listed → unverified, summary "Generated by AI from its training data — verify before booking."): - flights: all results source not estimate → verified ("Live fares from Google Flights"); mixed → partial; all estimate → unverified ("Estimated fares — prices change; check the airline"). - hotels: enrichment sets hotel["link_verified"] = True when _search_url matched a listing by name, False when it searched and found nothing (untouched hotels beyond the enrich cap: key absent). verified if all searched found, partial if some, unverified if none; items_verified/items_total over searched hotels; check line "Found online by name: X of N". First (pre-enrich) yield → pending: true, level unverified. - activities: resolver marks link_verified = True on activities it upgraded to a trusted listing domain (getyourguide/viator/klook/tripadvisor/tiqets/musement); partial if any, else unverified with detail "Links are searches, not specific listings". Prices/ratings always an info check "Prices and ratings are AI estimates". Pending on first yield when enrichment will run. - places_to_see: resolver marks link_verified = True when it set info_url from a search result; same partial/unverified logic. - walking_tours: verified ("Listings crawled from the providers' own pages"), one pass check per sources[] entry with status ok (url included); providers that failed → info. - weather: source == 'open-meteo' → verified ("Open-Meteo forecast/climate data"); contains llm-estimate → partial or unverified accordingly. - visa: static-first. Phase-0 static yield → verified, label "Verified", check "Matches our reference table" + official_url. AI yield: if get_static_visa(request) exists — same visa_type (normalised: lowercase, hyphen/space-insensitive) → verified; different → conflict, summary "AI says ; our reference table says . Check the official site.", check status fail with the official_url; never override the AI data. No table entry → unverified ("No reference data for this nationality and destination — confirm on the official site", url = data official_url when present). - emergency_card: compare emergency_numbers.police/ambulance/fire with the static table for the destination when present: all equal → verified; any differ → conflict naming the field and both values; no table → unverified. - static-backed sim / tips / getting_around / forex Phase-0 yields: verified label "Reference data" is NOT used — level verified, label "Verified", summary "From our curated reference data (may lag recent changes)". Their AI yields → unverified. - itinerary, stress_test, packing_list, events, pricing_advisor: unverified (events add an info check per date_certainty distribution, e.g. "3 of 5 dates confirmed annual"). - Error results ({"error": …}) get no verification (unchanged behaviour; cacheability unaffected — never put a key named error in verification).

Orchestrator: one helper _attach_verification(name, data, request, pending=False) called right before every section yield listed in orchestrator.py (Phase 0 static yields, Phase 1 ai yield with pending=True for agents that have enrich, itinerary, stress_test, packing_list (static and ai), pricing_advisor, enriched re-yield with pending=False). Mutating data in place is acceptable only if the same dict isn't reused elsewhere; otherwise copy (implementer checks enrich input reuse).

Frontend: - frontend/src/components/VerificationBadge.jsx: chip (emerald Verified / amber Partly verified / gray AI-generated / rose Check details; "Checking…" spinner when pending), button opening an accessible popover (Escape closes, focus returns) listing checks with pass/fail/info icons and links via safeUrl. - SectionHeader in frontend/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx renders it for results[agent]?.verification (before the status icons). Static → AI transitions just re-render with the new object. - Per-item "Found online" emerald micro-badge on hotel, activity and place cards when link_verified === true (no badge otherwise — absence is not an accusation). - The section-level conflict also shows as a one-line rose banner inside the Visa / Emergency section body with the official link. - Chat untouched (knowledge-only; chat emitter doesn't call the helper).

Non-goals: new network checks, LLM verifier, chat, exporting labels, changing which data is shown.

  3. Cached search replay — verification present and identical (it's inside data).
  4. Static → AI → enriched sequence — chip moves Checking… → final without flicker to a wrong level.
  5. Sections with {error} or missing lists — no verification, no crash.

docs.title: Backend Hardening: Exact Reference Lookups + Rate Limiting — Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: (1) Reference-table lookups (visa, destination scores, emergency numbers, anything using _match_destination / _find_dest_key in backend/app/agents/static_results.py) match only the right row, so "Verified" labels and Travel Ease scores can't come from a wrong row. (2) Expensive endpoints are rate-limited per user (or per client IP when anonymous) with a clear 429 + Retry-After, and the frontend shows a friendly message.

Architecture: A shared normaliser turns a destination string ("Barcelona, Spain", "BCN — Barcelona, Spain", "tokyo") into candidate place tokens (city, country) and lookups compare whole tokens against table keys and the city→country map — no substring matching in either direction. A small in-process sliding-window limiter (backend/app/core/rate_limit.py) is applied as a FastAPI dependency on expensive routes; limits come from settings; cache hits still count (simplicity) but limits are generous.

Spec: Follow-ups from the 2026-10-29 reviews ("fuzzy static lookups", "no rate limiting anywhere"). Design choices are Claude's (user delegated).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Lookups: - normalise_place(destination) -> {"city": str|None, "country": str|None, "tokens": set[str]}: lowercase; strip an IATA prefix like "BCN — "; split on commas; first segment = city (or country if it is itself a known country key); last segment = country when ≥2 segments; tokens = whole words/phrases of those segments. - A table key matches when it equals the normalised city, the normalised country, or the country mapped from the city via the existing city→country map (merge the two duplicated maps in _find_dest_key and _match_destination into ONE module-level map). Never key in dest / dest in key. - Nationality matching for _VISA_TABLE: exact match of the normalised nationality (lowercase, trimmed; accept the demonym forms already used in the table) — no substring (tbl_nat in nat is removed). - Behaviour for every currently-correct input must not change: build a regression test over all existing table keys and a list of realistic inputs (city, "City, Country", "IATA — City, Country", country alone, mixed case) asserting the same row as before; plus negative tests that used to match wrongly (e.g. a destination containing a table key as a substring of another word, "Indian" vs "American Indian"-style nationality substrings, short keys like "uk" inside "ukraine", "india" inside "indiana", "niger" inside "nigeria").

Rate limiting: - Sliding-window counter per key user:<username> or ip:<client host>; in-memory, thread-safe enough for asyncio (single process); old timestamps pruned. - Settings (pydantic-settings, env overridable): rate_limit_enabled: bool = True, and per-bucket limits: search 10/10min (POST /api/search, /api/search/sync), chat 30/10min (POST /api/chat), compare 30/10min (POST /api/compare/destination), discover 10/10min, light_ai 60/10min (POST /api/stress-test, /api/{flights,hotels,activities}/filtered and other single-agent POST routes in main.py that call an LLM). - Over the limit → HTTP 429, JSON {"detail": "Too many requests — please wait N seconds and try again."}, header Retry-After: N. - Tests: conftest disables limiting by default (env RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false) so existing tests are unaffected; dedicated tests enable it via settings override and assert 429 + Retry-After after N+1 calls, separate users don't share buckets, window expiry (inject a clock). - Frontend: wherever these calls surface errors — frontend/src/workers/sseWorker.js / services/api.js streamSearch error path, chat worker, compare (compareErrorReason already shows string detail), axios helpers — a 429 shows the server's detail string (no raw JSON). Add/extend unit tests where a helper exists. - Docs: CLAUDE.md (API section note), docs/API-Reference.md (429 behaviour + limits), docs/Configuration.md (settings).

Non-goals: distributed rate limiting, per-plan quotas, changing table contents.

docs.title: Budget Planner (Interactive Budget Slider) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: A "Budget planner" panel on the Results page that splits the trip budget into Flights / Stay / Activities / Everything else with sliders, instantly shows which loaded options fit each share, and can fetch cheaper hotels when too few fit.

Spec: Backlog #16 (Future_Improvements.md). Facts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/research-16-18-9.md (#16 section). Choices are Claude's (user delegated).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) slider drives /api/*/filtered (LLM re-run, 3–10 s each) — rejected as the primary mechanism: too slow for a slider and replaces the result lists; (b) client-side caps over already-loaded results — chosen, instant; the existing hotel filter endpoint is used only on demand ("Find cheaper hotels").

Model (pure util frontend/src/utils/budgetPlanner.js, unit-tested, // @vitest-environment node): - Units: the same per-person convention as the My Plan drawer and best-value package (flight price_usd per person; hotel nightly × nights; activity price_usd). Total = searchData.budget_usd (editable in the panel; not saved back to the search). - defaultAllocation(searchData, results) → { flights, stay, activities, other } summing exactly to the budget (integers, remainder to other): flights = cheapest valid fare (min with multi-city legs summed), stay = median nightly of priced hotels × nights, activities = 15% of budget, other = rest; if those exceed the budget, scale flights/stay/activities proportionally so other ≥ 0. No budget → panel hidden. - reallocate(allocation, key, value, total) → moving one category takes from / gives to other first; if other would go below 0, the change is clamped. Total stays constant. - fitResults(results, allocation, searchData) → { hotels: {fits:Set(name), count, total}, flights: {fits:Set(identity), count, total}, activities: {picked:Set(name), spent}, nights }: hotel fits when nightly × nights ≤ stay; flight fits when price ≤ flights (multi-city: per-leg fare ≤ flights share × leg's share of the cheapest total); activities: greedy pick by similarity_score desc (ties price asc) while cumulative price ≤ activities share; free ones always fit. Junk prices are "unknown" → never counted as fitting and never dimmed. - Edge: nights from dates (min 1, default 7) like planHelpers.

UI (frontend/src/components/BudgetPlanner.jsx + test): - Placed directly after the Best-value package card (only when isDone and budget > 0), collapsible (default expanded on desktop, collapsed below 640px). - Editable total (number input) + stacked bar (Flights sky, Stay purple, Activities green, Everything else gray — same colours as CostBreakdown) + three labelled range sliders (step $10) with values and "per person" note; "Everything else" shown read-only with a hint "food, transport, extras". - Under each slider: "6 of 12 hotels fit" / "4 of 9 flights fit" / "Fits 5 activities ($212)". - Toggle "Show only what fits" (default off). Off: over-budget hotel/flight cards are dimmed (opacity) with a small "Over your stay budget" / "Over your flight budget" tag; on: they are hidden with a "N hidden — show all" row. Activities picked by the planner get a "Fits your budget" tag. - When fewer than 3 hotels fit: button "Find cheaper hotels" → calls the existing handleApplyHotelFilters({ max_price_per_night_usd: floor(stay / nights) }) path (existing loading state, badge, verification). - "Reset" restores defaultAllocation. - Allocation state lives in ResultsPage, resets on new search/remix and when results for flights/hotels change (recompute default only if the user hasn't moved a slider). - Best-value package: buildBestValuePackage(results, searchData, { caps }) — when caps provided, hotel candidates limited to those that fit (fallback to current behaviour if none fit) and flight pool limited to fitting fares (fallback likewise); ResultsPage passes caps only when the user has touched the planner. Existing package tests must pass unchanged; add tests for caps. - Accessibility: sliders are <input type="range"> with aria-valuetext "$1,200 for stay"; changes announced politely ("Stay budget $1,200 — 5 of 12 hotels fit"). - Analytics: track('budget_planner_changed', 'results', { key }) (debounced), track('budget_planner_cheaper_hotels', 'results', {}). - Docs: Frontend.md paragraph; CLAUDE.md one line.

Non-goals: saving the allocation in plans, chat, multiplying by travellers, LLM calls from slider moves.

Comprehensive Airport & Place Data Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Replace the hand-typed 544-airport list with a comprehensive, regenerable dataset (OurAirports scheduled airports + GeoNames places ≥1,000 people) so any typed city, town, airport or alternate spelling resolves to the right airports and country — and close the remaining open items from PRs #17/#18.

Spec: User request 2026-10-30: "address the remaining items … make the airport data VERY VERY COMPREHENSIVE … VERY IMPORTANT AND CRITICAL FOR THE ENTIRE APPLICATION". The user approved downloading OurAirports (airports/regions/countries CSV, public domain) and GeoNames cities1000 + admin1CodesASCII (CC BY 4.0). Choices otherwise Claude's.

docs.title: Source data (already downloaded — untrusted input, read with python3 -I, never executed)
docs.text:
• OurAirports: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/ourairports-src/{airports,regions,countries}.csv (snapshot 2026-10-29).
  • GeoNames: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/geonames-src/extracted/cities1000.txt (171,731 rows, tab-separated, standard GeoNames columns) and …/geonames-src/admin1CodesASCII.txt.
  • Prototype showing the linking approach works: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rupak-travel-planner/6a423640-de0e-4ae7-a160-af5d4cd4d6e9/scratchpad/oa-scripts/proto.py (reference only; known flaws listed below are fixed by this design).

docs.title: Verified facts that drive the design
docs.text:
• OurAirports municipality is the physical location, not the city served: MXP "Ferno (VA)", BRU "Zaventem", CCS "Maiquetía", LEJ "Schkeuditz", SYD "Sydney (Mascot)", CDG "Paris (Roissy-en-France, Val-d'Oise)". Never use it alone as the served city.
  • OurAirports type is not a size signal (PWM, BHM, VLN, HHN are all large_airport).
  • 9,052 OA rows have IATA codes; 4,010 are large/medium/small with scheduled_service=yes (use these; heliports/seaplane bases excluded).
  • The curated list (backend/app/db/seed_airports.py) has stale/wrong codes: PNH/REP (closed, replaced by KTI/SAI), KBP/IEV/LWO/ODS (no scheduled service), ULN→UBN, DKR→DSS, KIV (OA: RMO), TIP (OA: MJI), NIY (Freetown is FNA), PBI (OA lists KPBI with IATA DJT). OA is authoritative for codes, names, coordinates, region and scheduled status; the curated list is authoritative only for the served-city display name of its airports and as the "tier 0" name layer.
  • GeoNames alternate names cause false hits if treated like primary names (prototype: "Cancun"→Changchun, "Venice"→Dayton, "Bali"→Bari).
  • Population alone mis-ranks namesakes; population × notability fixes them (data checked): score = population × (alternate_name_count + 1)² × (3 if feature code PPLC). Results at a 3× dominance threshold: Interlaken→CH, Venice→IT, Victoria→CA (not the HK district), Portland→US-OR, Birmingham→GB, Paris/Rome/Athens/Florence/Naples/Sydney/Melbourne/Perth→the famous one; Valencia, Cambridge, Toledo, Hamilton, San Jose, Springfield→ambiguous.
  • get_connection() returns a raw sqlite3.Connection; with conn: commits but never closes (connections leak until GC).

docs.title: A. Generator (backend/scripts/build_place_data.py, stdlib only, deterministic output, run manually; never at app runtime)
docs.text:
Inputs: paths to the OA and GeoNames files + the curated AIRPORTS list. Outputs (committed): 1. backend/app/db/data/airports.csv — one row per airport: every OA large/medium/small airport with scheduled_service=yes and an IATA code, plus every curated code (curated codes not scheduled in OA kept with scheduled=0). Columns: iata, icao, name, city, country, country_code, region (OA iso_region, e.g. US-OR), type_rank (0 large,1 medium,2 small,9 other), scheduled (1/0), lat, lng. country = OA countries.csv name, except keep the curated spelling for curated airports' countries (so existing displays like "United States"/"United Kingdom" don't change). city (display) = curated city when curated; else the highest-scoring place that links this airport (below) within 80 km; else the cleaned municipality (text before the first "(" or ","; for "A/B" keep "A"). 2. backend/app/db/data/places.csv.gz — one row per GeoNames place with feature code not in {PPLX, PPLH, PPLQ, PPLW, PPLCH}: geonameid, name, country_code, admin1, population, score, lat, lng, airports (space-separated IATA, ranked, ≤3), alt_names ("|"-joined folded names). Alt names: Latin-script only, ≤40 chars, not URLs/codes (all-uppercase ≤4 chars), folded, de-duplicated, excluding the place's own folded name; keep them only for places with population ≥ 15,000 (size control). Notability count for score uses the raw alternate-name count. 3. backend/app/db/data/admin1.csv — code (e.g. US.OR, CA.08, AU.08, DE.02, GB.ENG), name, folded_name from admin1CodesASCII. 4. A conflict report printed to stdout (not committed): curated codes missing/unscheduled in OA, curated vs OA country mismatches, airports whose display city fell back to municipality for type_rank 0.

Linking (place → airports), scheduled airports only: - Reach per airport type: large 80 km (100 km when place population ≥ 1,000,000 and no large airport is within 50 km), medium 50 km, small 30 km. Rank linked airports by (type_rank, distance); keep ≤3. - No airport in reach → nearest large/medium within 150 km (≤2). Still none → empty. - Folding (shared with runtime, see C): NFKD strip combining marks; ß→ss ø→o æ→ae œ→oe ł→l đ→d ı→i þ→th ð→d; lower-case; "." and "-" → space; collapse whitespace.

docs.title: B. Storage & seeding (backend/app/db/database.py, backend/app/db/seed_airports.py)
docs.text:
• Schema: airports gains region TEXT, type_rank INTEGER, scheduled INTEGER DEFAULT 1 (migrate existing DBs with ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN when missing). New tables: places(geonameid PK, name, country_code, admin1, population, score, lat, lng, airports), place_names(name_folded, geonameid, tier) with an index on name_folded (tier 0 = primary/ascii name, 1 = alternate), admin1(code PK, name, folded_name), meta(key PK, value).
  • Versioned seeding: PLACE_DATA_VERSION = hash of the three data files (computed once, cheap) stored in meta. On startup, when the stored version differs: in ONE transaction upsert all dataset airports (INSERT … ON CONFLICT(iata_code) DO UPDATE), leave rows not in the dataset (web-saved) untouched but set their scheduled to 1 only if unknown, and rebuild places/place_names/admin1. Equal version → skip (fast startup). Startup log line with counts and seconds.
  • get_connection() closes connections: make it a context manager (@contextmanager) that yields the connection, commits on success, rolls back on error and always closes. Every caller in backend/app must keep working (grep all callers; the with get_connection() as conn: pattern stays valid).
  • Tests: the suite must not get meaningfully slower (≤ +15% wall time). Seed the place data once per session (session fixture / shared seeded DB file copied per test DB if tests use separate DBs), not per test.
  • Drop the per-airport curated AIRPORT_REGION map in favour of the dataset region, keeping only the deliberate extras as an overrides table (IAD/DCA also "dc", MCI also "ks"); existing region tests must stay green.

docs.title: C. Resolution (backend/app/core/places.py, lookup_city_iata, static_results._place_country)
docs.text:
• One shared fold_place (A) and one consolidated country alias map in core/places.py (merge database._COUNTRY_CODE_ALIASES and the static_results country aliases; both modules import it).
  • resolve_place(text) -> Place | None in a new backend/app/db/places_db.py (one indexed query for names + one for admin1 when a region is stated):
  • Parse: strip a known-airport-code prefix ("BER — …"), split city / stated last segment. Stated segment may be a country (name/alias/ISO), a US/CA/AU/BR region code (existing tables), or an admin1 name (any country, folded, e.g. "Bavaria", "Ontario", "New South Wales", "England").
  • Candidates: places whose tier-0 name equals the folded city (also try St./Saint variants); only if none, tier-1 (alternate) matches.
  • Filter by the stated country/region (region via admin1 code or name; a code with several readings keeps every reading's places). Stated country with no candidates in it → None.
  • Curated hint: if _CITY_TO_COUNTRY (curated city map) names a country for this city and candidates exist in it, keep only those.
  • Winner: highest score if ≥ 3× the next candidate's score; else None (ambiguous).
  • lookup_city_iata(text) order: bare code → known-code prefix → curated tier (today's curated-name logic over curated airports, excluding airports with scheduled=0) giving codes in curated order → then place resolution; when both apply to the same city, curated codes first then the place's linked airports, de-duplicated, ≤3. Never return scheduled=0 airports. Unknown → None.
  • static_results._place_country: unchanged curated logic first; when it returns None for an unknown city (not for an explicit "no row" ruling like "Paris, TX"), fall back to resolve_place and map its country code through the ISO→table map (only countries present in the tables). Rulings that must hold: "Paris, Texas"/"Paris, TX" → None; "Tbilisi, Georgia" → None or georgia-if-in-tables (never usa); "Denver, CO" → usa; "Smalltown, CO" → None.
  • search_airports (autocomplete): also match places by folded name prefix and return their linked airports; order: exact code, code prefix, exact city/place name, prefix, other; within a class by type_rank then name; exclude scheduled=0 unless the code was typed exactly. Response shape unchanged.

docs.title: D. Expected behaviour (tests must pin all of these)
docs.text:
• Airports: "Milan"/"Milano" → LIN/MXP/BGY set incl. MXP; "Brussels" → BRU first; "Caracas" → CCS; "Frankfurt" → FRA only (HHN excluded: 115 km); "Paris" → CDG,ORY first (curated order); "London" → LHR,LGW,STN (curated order); "New York" → JFK,LGA,EWR; "Tokyo" → HND/NRT; "Washington" → starts IAD,DCA (curated) ; "Kyoto" → ITM and/or KIX; "Ubud" → DPS; "Zermatt"/"Interlaken" → nearest scheduled airports (BRN/ZRH/GVA/SIR region — assert non-empty and Swiss/nearby); "Bombay" → BOM; "Saigon" → SGN; "München" → MUC; "Lisboa" → LIS; "Phnom Penh" → KTI (not PNH); "Siem Reap" → SAI (not REP); "Chisinau"/"Chișinău" → RMO; "London, ON"/"London, Ontario" → YXU; "Sydney, Nova Scotia" → YQY; "Portland" → PDX (dominance; changes the old None ruling — update that test); "Portland, ME" → PWM; "Birmingham" → BHX; "Birmingham, AL" → BHM; "Valencia" → None; "Valencia, Spain" → VLC; "San Jose" → None; "Springfield" → None; "Springfield, IL" → SPI if scheduled in data; "Venice" → VCE/TSF; "Interlaken, Switzerland" non-empty; "Cancun" → CUN; "Bali" → DPS (curated); "Munich, Bavaria" → MUC; "Perth, WA" → PER; "Seattle, WA" → SEA; "Kansas City, KS" → MCI; "St Louis" → STL; "Paris, Texas" → None or PRX-if-scheduled (never CDG); "Toronto, CA" → YYZ; bare "NYC" → NYC; "LGW — London, …" → LGW.
  • Countries (_place_country): "St Petersburg" → russia; "Zermatt" → switzerland; "Ubud" → indonesia; "Hallstatt" → austria only if present in cities1000 else None; "Kyoto" → japan; "Interlaken" → switzerland; "Venice" → italy; all existing static-lookup tests green.
  • Autocomplete: "milan" → MXP/LIN/BGY with city "Milan"; "kyoto" → returns ITM/KIX; "zermatt" non-empty; "lhr" → LHR first; "lon" → London airports before e.g. Long Beach.

docs.title: E. Remaining open items (close or rule explicitly in the report)
docs.text:
• Accented web-saved rows: folded names apply to every airport row (dataset or web) via place_names/folded city matching.
  • Washington handled (curated + places); St Petersburg static row (via fallback); London, Ontario (data); connections closed (B); duplicate alias maps (C).
  • Sync SQLite in async handlers: keep sync (sub-millisecond indexed reads) — document the measured lookup time in the report.

Docs: backend/app/db/data/README.md (sources, licences — OurAirports public domain, GeoNames CC BY 4.0 attribution "Contains data from GeoNames (geonames.org), CC BY 4.0" — snapshot date, exact regeneration command, conflict-report summary); Architecture/API docs lines on place resolution; CLAUDE.md one line under Key Conventions.

Fare Calendar Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Show whether today's fares are low/typical/high (from data Google Flights already returns), and an opt-in strip of the cheapest real fare for departure dates ±3 days (same trip length), with one click to re-plan on a cheaper date.

Spec: Backlog #9. Facts: research-16-18-9.md (#9 section). Choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) LLM-estimated date grid — rejected (fabricated numbers; contradicts the verification rule); (b) 7×7 departure×return grid — rejected (49 SerpAPI calls); (c) price_insights from existing responses (0 extra calls) + opt-in ±3-day departure strip keeping trip length (6 extra calls, cached) — chosen.

Backend: - serp_flights.py: capture price_insights from the outbound search response (lowest_price, price_level, typical_price_range, price_history) and include it in the flights result as price_insights (single-city only); absent → omitted. Not cached separately (rides with the result). Verification for flights unchanged. - New search_calendar(api_key, request, window=3) in serp_flights.py: for each offset in −3..+3 (skip dates before tomorrow; skip offset 0 if the main search result is cached — reuse it), build params via _build_params(request.model_copy(update={departure_date, return_date shifted by the same offset})), ONE outbound call per date (no return-leg calls), cheapest price across best/other flights; concurrency limited (semaphore 4); per-date cache key serp-cal:{origin}:{dest}:{dep}:{ret}:{adults} (30-min TTL, shared cache); a failed date → null price, not an error. - Route POST /api/flights/fare-calendar (auth required like other routes; light_ai rate-limit bucket from the hardening branch if present, else no limiter) body = TravelSearchRequest; 422 for multi-city; 503 {"detail": "Fare calendar needs live flight data, which isn't configured."} when settings.serpapi_key is empty; response { dates: [{ departure_date, return_date, cheapest_usd|null, is_selected }], currency: "USD", source: "google_flights" }. - Tests: mocked _call (no network) — window dates, past-date skipping, null on failure, cache hit, 422/503/401, price_insights passthrough.

Frontend: - Flights section: when results.flights.price_insights exists, a chip under the pricing banner: "Fares are low right now · typical $420–$610" (green/gray/amber for low/typical/high) — real data, linked to the verification idea (no AI). - "Fare calendar" pill in the Flights header actions (next to Filters) shown only when /health reports serpapi_configured (fetch once; cache in module) and the trip is single-city. Click → loads FareCalendarStrip below the banner: 7 cells (weekday, date, price or "—"), cheapest highlighted emerald, selected date outlined, delta vs selected ("−$45"). Loading skeleton; error row with Retry (string detail via existing error helpers; 429 detail shown). - Clicking a different date opens an inline confirm: "Re-plan for Tue 3 Nov – Tue 10 Nov? This runs a new search." → on confirm, runSearch({...searchData, departure_date, return_date}) (existing full search path; selections reset as with Remix) and track('fare_calendar_replan', 'results', { offset }). - Pure helpers in frontend/src/utils/fareCalendar.js (shiftDates, cheapest/delta, formatting) + tests; component FareCalendarStrip.jsx + test. - Fix the PricingAdvisorBanner date bug noted in research (it parses the destination as a date) since we touch this area: use searchData.departure_date. - Docs: API-Reference (endpoint), Frontend.md, CLAUDE.md API table.

Non-goals: multi-city calendars, return-date grid, LLM fallback grid, price alerts.

Goal: (1) Close the accessibility gaps left in the itinerary editor and Results section headers. (2) Let users re-run the Trip Health Check against their edited itinerary.

Spec: Follow-ups from the 2026-10-29 reviews. Design choices are Claude's (user delegated).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Accessibility: - Results SectionHeader (frontend/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx) is a clickable div: make the collapse toggle keyboard-operable — a real <button> for the title/toggle area with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the section body id; the VerificationBadge chip and any actions stay outside that button (no nested interactive elements); clicking the chip must not toggle (keep the existing stopPropagation). - ItinerarySection (frontend/src/components/ItinerarySection.jsx): per-row action buttons get accessible names including the activity — Edit <activity>, Add note to <activity> / Edit note for <activity>, Add <activity> to plan / Remove <activity> from plan (visible text unchanged); the Removed list's Restore buttons Restore <activity>. - VerificationBadge: add the missing Shift+Tab-from-container test.

Health Check re-run: - When layoutChangeCount > 0, StressTestSection shows, next to the existing note, a button "Re-check my edited plan". It POSTs to /api/stress-test with the current search request plus itinerary = the ARRANGED itinerary (arrangeItinerary with edits applied: each slot's activity/location/cost use itinerary_edits overrides; removed activities excluded), and flights/visa/weather from current results (strip verification objects before sending). - While running: button disabled with spinner ("Re-checking…"). Result replaces the displayed findings in place (do not mutate results.stress_test; keep a separate recheck state holding {data, forLayoutFingerprint}), with the heading note "Checked against your edited itinerary". If the layout or edits change afterwards, show "Your plan changed since this check — re-check again" and the button again. - Errors (incl. 429): show the server's string detail or "Couldn't re-check — try again", keep the previous findings. - recheck state clears on new search / loaded plan / Reset. - Pure helper buildStressTestPayload(searchData, results, selections) in frontend/src/utils/ with unit tests (arranged days, edits applied, removed excluded, verification stripped, return_date normalised via existing apiReturnDate). - Docs: docs/Frontend.md Health Check paragraph.

Non-goals: auto re-check, chat.

docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Close the four follow-ups parked after PR #17: a US/CA/AU/BR state narrows a city's airports ("Portland, OR" → PDX only), Washington spellings resolve, accented input resolves, and the fare calendar's selected-date price agrees with the flight cards.

Spec: User request 2026-10-30 ("these are things we should explicitly account for and resolve"). Facts gathered by the controller are listed under each item. Choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Facts (verified against the seed and code)
docs.text:
• backend/app/db/seed_airports.py: 544 airports; city names are ASCII-folded ("Sao Paulo", "Zurich", "Montreal", "Krakow", "Reykjavik", "Malmo", "Dusseldorf", "Bogota", "Medellin"); the only non-ASCII city is "Ålesund". No state/region column. US 81, CA 11, AU 11, BR 10 airports.
  • Same-name cities more than 60 km apart: within one country only "portland" (PDX/US, PWM/US, 4070 km); across countries birmingham, san jose, victoria (already None via the country-code ambiguity rule).
  • Washington is stored as city "Washington D.C." (IAD, DCA); BWI is a separate city. "St. Petersburg" is stored with the period; "New York" (JFK, LGA).
  • Fare calendar (serp_flights.search_calendar): non-selected dates use _cheapest(outbound response) (the cheapest price from the first, outbound-stage call). The selected date uses _cached_selected_price(main), which prefers Google's price_insights.lowest_price. Flight cards are return-stage round-trip totals (_map_result on return items). Observed live: selected $360 (lowest_price) vs cheapest card $341.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
1. State/region narrows airports (lookup_city_iata):
  2. Add a curated AIRPORT_REGION: dict[str, str] (IATA → region code: US state / CA province / AU state / BR UF, lower-case 2–3 letters matching core/places.py region codes) covering every US, CA, AU and BR airport in the seed. A completeness test fails when a seed airport in those countries has no region. Put the map next to the seed data (e.g. backend/app/db/airport_regions.py); no DB schema change.
  3. When the stated last segment is a region code or US state name, keep only the rows whose AIRPORT_REGION equals that region; rows without region data (other countries, web rows) are dropped by a region filter.
  4. Same-country, far-apart matches: if the remaining rows span more than one region (by AIRPORT_REGION) and no region was stated, the city is ambiguous → None. ("Portland" → None; "Portland, OR" → PDX; "Portland, Maine" → PWM; "Portland, ME" → PWM.) Rows from countries without region data keep today's behaviour (London still → LHR,LGW,STN).

  5. Tests for each example above plus "Springfield, IL" when present in the seed (else skip), "Birmingham, AL" → BHM, "Birmingham, UK" → BHX, "San Jose, CA" → SJC, "Victoria, BC" → YYJ.

  6. City spelling normalisation (both lookup_city_iata and static_results.normalise_place / _place_country):

  7. One shared helper in backend/app/core/places.py: fold_place(text) -> str — NFKD + strip combining marks, plus explicit transliteration for ß→ss, ø→o, æ→ae, œ→oe, ł→l, đ→d, ı→i, þ→th, ð→d; lower-case, collapse whitespace.
  8. A small CITY_ALIASES map (folded alias → DB city spelling), at minimum: washington / washington dc / washington d c / washington d.c. / dc → "Washington D.C."; saint petersburg / st petersburg → "St. Petersburg"; new york city / nyc → "New York" (only when not a bare code — the bare-code path wins for "NYC"); saigon → "Ho Chi Minh City"; bombay → "Mumbai". Verify each target exists in the seed (test).
  9. lookup_city_iata queries city IN (:typed, :folded, :alias) with COLLATE NOCASE (still indexed, one query). "Ålesund" must still match when typed with or without the ring.
  10. _place_country: fold the city before the city-map lookup and fold the map keys once (accented keys like "são paulo" stay valid). "Zürich" / "Zurich, Switzerland" / "São Paulo, BR" / "Washington" / "Washington DC" / "Washington, D.C." all resolve (switzerland / brazil / usa). "Washington" alone must not become ambiguous with the US state name — usa either way.

  11. Tests: "São Paulo" → GRU (+ others in the seed), "Zürich" → ZRH, "Düsseldorf" → DUS, "Kraków" → KRK, "Malmö" → MMX, "Reykjavík" → RKV (+KEF if seeded as Reykjavik), "Washington" / "Washington, DC" / "Washington D.C." → IAD,DCA, "Saint Petersburg" → LED, "St Petersburg" → LED, "Ålesund"/"Alesund" → AES.

  12. Fare calendar selected-date price agrees with the cards (serp_flights.py):

  13. The main round-trip / one-way search records the cheapest outbound-stage price (_cheapest(data1) / _cheapest(data)) for its dates when it ran unfiltered, by writing the per-date calendar cache entry the calendar already reads (serp-cal: key, same format as search_calendar uses).
  14. search_calendar selected date: min(cheapest outbound-stage price for that date, cheapest mapped card price from the cached main search), either may be missing; fall back to Google's lowest_price only when both are missing. Update _cached_selected_price and its docstring accordingly; non-selected dates unchanged.
  15. Tests (mocked _call): main search writes the cal cache entry when unfiltered and not when filtered; selected date = cheapest card when the cards are cheaper than lowest_price (the $341 vs $360 case); selected date = outbound cheapest when no cards; lowest_price only when neither exists; existing calendar tests stay green.

Docs: API-Reference / Agent-System lines that describe city resolution and the fare calendar.

For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: (1) Free-text cities ("Berlin", "Berlin, Germany", "BER — Berlin, Germany") get real airport codes for live flight search and the fare calendar. (2) "City, XX" where XX is an ISO country code resolves to that country in the reference tables. (3) The chat itinerary prompt asks for durations and coordinates like the main itinerary prompt.

Spec: Follow-ups surfaced on 2026-10-30. Choices are Claude's (user delegated).

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
1. City → airport codes (backend):
  2. Where: the TravelSearchRequest validator that today resolves 3-letter codes (backend/app/schemas/request.py resolve_iata_codes, origin_iata / destination_iata excluded fields) — extend it so that when origin/destination is NOT already a code, it looks the place up in the local airports database (the same data /api/airports/search serves; find the DB helper in backend/app/db/) by city name: first comma segment (after stripping a leading "XXX — " prefix), case-insensitive exact city match; if a country is given (last comma segment), restrict to that country (accept common names/aliases the DB uses); pick up to 3 airports in that city, primary/largest first if the DB has such a signal, else stable by code; set origin_iata/destination_iata to the comma-joined list (SerpAPI accepts comma lists for departure_id/arrival_id).
  3. Multi-city: apply the same to each destinations[] entry wherever the multi-city flight search reads codes (check serp_flights multi-city params builder).
  4. NEVER perform web/network lookups in this path (the existing web fallback for unknown 3-letter codes is untouched); unknown city → leave unset → today's behaviour (AI estimate).
  5. serp_flights._build_params (and the calendar) must use the resolved codes; verify the existing code already prefers origin_iata/destination_iata, otherwise wire it.
  6. Tests (DB seeded in tests as other tests do): "Berlin" → BER; "Berlin, Germany" → BER; "BER — Berlin, Germany" → BER; "London" → up to 3 London airports incl. LHR; "Paris, Texas" → none (no match in that country); "Springfield" ambiguity without country → pick only if all matches share one country, else none; codes passed through unchanged; _build_params uses the comma list; no network calls (monkeypatch any web helper to fail).
  7. ISO country codes in reference lookups (backend/app/agents/static_results.py _place_country / normaliser):
  8. Add an ISO-3166 alpha-2 → table-country map for every country present in the reference tables (and their aliases).
  9. Rule for a trailing ≤2-letter segment: if the city-map country for the city equals the ISO code's country → that country; else if the code is an ISO code and the city is unknown → that country; else if it's a US state code and the city-map says usa (or the city is unknown and the code is not an ISO country) → usa; otherwise no row. Examples (tests): "Berlin, DE" → germany; "Toronto, CA" → canada; "Bali, ID" → indonesia; "Delhi, IN" → india; "Miami, FL" → usa; "Paris, FR" → france; "Paris, TX" → no row; "Paris, Texas" → no row. The existing lookup regression suite must stay green.
  10. Chat itinerary prompt (backend/app/agents/chat_itinerary_agent.py): require duration_hours on every slot and lat/lng on every slot (approximate neighbourhood or hotel coordinates when there's no specific place), matching .agents/itinerary.md wording; prompt test like backend/tests/test_itinerary_timing_prompt.py.

Docs: API-Reference / Agent-System lines where these behaviours are described.

docs.title: Timed Itinerary (Minute-Level Scheduling) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax.

Goal: Every itinerary activity shows an estimated start–end time and the travel time from the previous stop; days that don't fit are flagged; times follow the user's drag-and-drop edits and flow into Timeline, calendar export, print, share and the Health Check re-check.

Spec: Backlog #18. Facts: research-16-18-9.md (#18 section) in the scratchpad. Choices are Claude's.

docs.title: Design (binding)
docs.text:
Options weighed: (a) LLM emits times — rejected: stale as soon as the user moves an activity, and unverifiable; (b) deterministic client-side scheduler applied after arrangeItinerary — chosen: one source of truth that re-runs on every edit; positions/keys (<day>-<time_of_day>) unchanged, so edits/notes/plan picks/.ics UIDs keep working.

Scheduler (pure frontend/src/utils/schedule.js, unit-tested, node env): - scheduleDays(days, edits = {}) -> days' (new objects) adding to each slot start_time "HH:MM", end_time, transit_from_prev: { minutes, mode: 'walk'|'transit', km } | null, and to each day schedule_warnings: string[]. - Bucket anchors: morning 09:00, afternoon 13:30, evening 18:30; slots ordered by existing rank (time_of_day order, odd slots by slotRanks rule — reuse helpers from itineraryLayout.js). - Duration: duration_hours (finite, 0.25–12) else defaults morning 3h / afternoon 3h / evening 2.5h; edits don't change duration. - Transit between consecutive slots: if both have finite lat/lng → km = haversine × 1.3; walk if km ≤ 1.5 (4.5 km/h), else transit (20 km/h + 10 min); minutes rounded up to 5; first slot of a day has no transit. Missing coords → transit_from_prev: null but scheduling assumes a 20-min buffer. - start = max(anchor, prev.end + transit/buffer); end = start + duration. - Warnings: start pushed > 45 min past its anchor → " starts at 14:20 — later than planned"; day ends after 23:00 → "Day N runs past 23:00". Days with no standard slots untouched. - Shared haversine: extract haversineKm from TripMap.jsx into frontend/src/utils/geo.js (TripMap imports it).

Wiring (renderers use scheduleDays(arrangeItinerary(...).days, edits)): - ItinerarySection: row shows "09:00–12:00" under the time-of-day label; between rows a muted transit line ("🚶 12 min walk · 0.9 km" / "🚇 ~25 min by transit" / nothing when unknown); a per-day amber "Tight schedule" chip listing warnings; a one-line note "Times are estimates based on typical durations and distances." - TimelineView: show times in each slot card. - planExport.js (.ics): use start_time/end_time when present (fallback SLOT_HOURS unchanged → existing tests stay green); planItineraryDays returns scheduled days. - planPrint.js, SharePage.jsx, PlanViewModal.jsx: show "09:00–12:00" next to time_of_day. - Stress-test re-check payload (utils/stressTestPayload.js from the polish branch): include start/end/transit; backend stress_test_agent._summarize_itinerary prints HH:MM–HH:MM and transit minutes when present (backend unit test). - Prompts: .agents/itinerary.md and backend/app/agents/itinerary_agent.py — require duration_hours on every slot and lat/lng on every slot that names a specific place (no other changes); backend fallback itinerary unchanged. - ChatPage unchanged. - Docs: Frontend.md, Agent-System.md one line.
